contributorNote: Gĩkũyũ (Kikuyu) vocabulary compiled from Lieut. Ludwig von Höhnel (1894 "Discovery of Lakes Rudolf and Stefanie"), Sir Harry H. Johnston (1902, 1919), Rev. Fr. A. Hémery, C.S.Sp. (1903 "English-Kikuyu Hand-Book", Zanzibar—Nairobi: Roman Catholic Mission, pp. 1–87 [PDF pp. 1–92]), Hildegarde Hinde (1904), Rev. A. W. McGregor (1904 "English-Kikuyu Vocabulary", C.M.S. / SPCK London, Fort Smith / Kabeti 1901–1902, pp. i–iv, 5–192 [PDF pp. 1–201]), W. Scoresby & Katherine Routledge (1910), C. W. Hobley (1910, 1922), Hon. Charles Dundas (1915), and BFBS (1921). Expanded and cross-verified with Commercially Permissive Datasets (The Thiomi Dataset (CC-BY-4.0), Google SMOL/GATITOS (en_kik, CC-BY-4.0), African Next Voices Kenya (5 Gikuyu dialects, CC-BY-4.0), CGIAR Kikuyu–English (Apache-2.0), LughaGen (CC-BY-SA-4.0), Mich-Seth Owusu Emotion & Parallel Corpora (MIT/CC-BY-4.0), CLDF Tsammalex & ASJP v20 (CC-BY-4.0), Kaikki.org (CC-BY-SA-4.0)).

entries.translation: Kĩririkano kĩa mũthuri ũcio mũkũrũ kĩarĩ na ngũĩ mũno, o ta ũrĩa kwagĩrĩire mũndũ watũrĩte maica mega.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The family and friends gathered around the coffin, telling stories and laughing about the good times they had shared with the deceased.
entries.translation: Andũ a nyũmba na arata marĩ ithandũkũ-inĩ, makĩganaga ng'ano na magĩthekaga nĩ ũndũ wa mahinda mega rĩrĩa marĩ na mũtigairĩ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: There was plenty of food and drink, and the music never stopped.
entries.translation: Nĩ kwarĩ na irio na inywanji nyingĩ mũno, na rwĩmbo rũtiatithirio ona rĩ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: At one point, the widow stood up and raised her glass.
entries.translation: Hindĩ ĩmwe, mũtumia ũcio wa ndigwa akĩrũgama na akĩoya ngirathi yake na igũrũ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: "To my husband," she said. "He was a good man, and he will be missed. But he's in a better place now, and we'll see him again someday."
entries.translation: "Kũrĩ mũthuri wakwa," akiuga. "Aarĩ mũndũ mwega, na nĩ ariririkanagwo. No ee handũ hega makĩria thaa ici, na nĩ tukonana nake mũthenya ũmwe."
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The crowd cheered and drank in unison.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The old man's spirit was there with them, and they knew that he would be happy to see them celebrating his life.
entries.translation: Roho wa mũthuri ũcio warĩ hamwe nao, na nĩ mamenyaga atĩ nĩ egũkena amona magĩkũngũĩra mũtũrĩre wake.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The wake went on for hours, and by the end of the night, everyone was exhausted but happy.
entries.translation: Kĩririkano kĩu gĩgĩthiĩ na mbere kwa mathaa, na gũgĩkinya ũtukũ, andũ othe marĩ anogu no nĩ makenete.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Your skin is your largest organ, and it's important to take care of it both inside and out. Here are some tips for healthy skin:
entries.translation: Ngothi yaku nĩyo kĩĩga kĩrĩa kĩnene mũno, na nĩ ũndũ wa bata kũmĩmenyerera thĩĩni na nja. Ngũkũhe motaaro megiĩ kũiga ngothi njega:
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: * Drink plenty of water: Water is essential for healthy skin, as it helps to keep your skin hydrated and soft. Aim to drink eight glasses of water per day.
entries.translation: * Nyua maaĩ maĩngĩ: Maaĩ nĩ ma bata mũno harĩ kũiga ngothi njega, nĩ mateithagia hari kũiga ngothi yaku ĩrĩ na maaĩ na ĩrĩ njororo. Ĩkĩrĩra kũnyua ngirathi inyanya cia maaĩ oo mũthenya.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: * Eat a healthy diet: Eating a healthy diet rich in fruits, vegetables, and whole grains can help to improve your skin's appearance.
entries.translation: * Rĩa irio njega: Kũrĩa irio njega iria irĩ na matunda, mboga, na irio cia mbegũ no citeithie harĩ kwambatĩria mũhaunire wa ngothi yaku.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: * Get regular exercise: Exercise can help to improve your circulation and promote healthy skin. Aim for at least 30 minutes of moderate-intensity exercise most days of the week.
entries.translation: * Ĩka mazoezi kaingĩ: Gũĩka mazoezi nĩ gũteithagia harĩ kwambatĩria ũnyagia wa thakame na kũrehe ngothi njega. Ĩkĩrĩra gũĩka mazoezi maritũ ma ndagĩka 30 thikũ nyingĩ cia kiumia.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: * Get enough sleep: When you don't get enough sleep, your body produces more of the stress hormone cortisol, which can lead to inflammation and skin problems. Aim for 7-8 hours of sleep per night.
entries.translation: * Koma toro mũiganu: Rĩrĩa waga gũkoma toro mũiganu, mwĩrĩ waku nĩ ũrutaga homoni nyingĩ cia mĩtangĩko nĩyo cortisol, ĩrĩa ĩngĩrehe kũimba na mathĩna ma ngothi. Ĩkĩrĩra mathaa 7-8 ma toro oo ũtukũ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: * Protect your skin from the sun: The sun's UV rays can damage your skin and lead to premature aging, wrinkles, and skin cancer.
entries.translation: * Gitĩra ngothi yaku kuumana na riũa: Mĩrũri ya riũa ya UV no ĩthũkie ngothi yaku na ĩcũngĩrĩrie gũkũra gũtakinyanĩire, mĩgutha, na kansa ya ngothi.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: But in 1974, a military junta known as the Derg seized power and began a brutal campaign of repression.
entries.translation: No mwaka-inĩ wa 1974, gĩkundi kĩa jeshi kĩũĩkaine ta Derg nĩkĩegwatĩire wathani na gĩkĩambia kambĩinĩ njũru ya kũhinyanĩrĩria.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The Derg's policies led to widespread famine and poverty, and millions of Ethiopians were forced to flee their homes.
entries.translation: Mĩtaratara ya Derg nĩ ya cũngĩrĩirie ng'aragũ nene na ũkia, na mamirioni ma aikari a Ethiopia makĩũra kuuma mĩciĩ yao.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: In 1991, a coalition of rebel groups known as the Ethiopian People's Revolutionary Democratic Front (EPRDF) overthrew the Derg.
entries.translation: Mwaka-inĩ wa 1991, mũũngano wa ikundi cia ĩtoĩ ũĩkanine ta Ethiopian People's Revolutionary Democratic Front (EPRDF) ũkĩhagũra Derg.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The EPRDF established a new government and promised to restore peace and prosperity to Ethiopia.
entries.translation: Gĩkundi kĩa EPRDF gĩgĩthondeka thĩrikari njerũ na gĩkĩĩranĩra gũcokia thayũ na ũgacĩru Ethiopia.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: However, the EPRDF's rule has been plagued by human rights abuses, corruption, and political repression.
entries.translation: Ona kũrĩ ũgũo, wathani wa EPRDF nĩ wahotomĩrio nĩ ũnyarari wa ihoto cia ũmũndũ, ungumania, na ũhinyĩrĩria wa maũndũ ma ũteti.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: In 2018, Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed took office and pledged to reform the country.
entries.translation: Mwaka-inĩ wa 2018, Mũtongoria wa thirikari Abiy Ahmed akĩoya wathani na akĩĩranĩra kũgarũra bũrũri ũcio.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: He released political prisoners, lifted restrictions on the media, and began peace talks with the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF), the former ruling party of Tigray.
entries.translation: Akĩohora ohwo a kĩ-ũteti, akĩeheria mĩhĩnga ya ũmemerekia, na akĩanjia mĩario ya thayu na Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF), kĩama kĩrĩa kĩarĩ wathani-inĩ mwena wa Tigray.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: However, the peace talks broke down in June 2020, and the TPLF launched an offensive against the Ethiopian military.
entries.translation: O na kũrĩ ũguo, mĩario ĩyo ĩkĩharagana mweri-inĩ wa Gatandatu 2020, na TPLF magĩbanga gũtharĩkĩra mbirarũ cia Ethiopia.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The ensuing conflict has been devastating.
entries.translation: Ngũcanio ĩyo ĩrĩa yacũngĩrĩire ĩkoretwo ĩrĩ njũru mũno.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The fighting has displaced millions of people, and the humanitarian situation is dire.
entries.translation: Mbaara ĩyo nĩ ĩtigĩte mamirioni ma andũ matarĩ na ũikaro, na kĩhonia kĩa ũmũndũ nĩ kĩrabatarania.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: It’s coming from the kitchen, so I get up to investigate.
entries.translation: Urauma riko, kũoguo ngĩũkĩra na ngĩthiĩ gũtuĩria.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: I creep down the hallway, careful not to make a sound.
entries.translation: Ngĩkumĩrĩra kahora njĩra-inĩ, na ũbacĩrĩri ndikaiguike.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)
Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: I peer around the corner into the kitchen and see Mum standing at the sink, staring out the window.
entries.translation: Ngĩrorera mwena wa kona wa riko na ngĩona Mami arũgamĩte indo-inĩ, arorete ndirica-inĩ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: She looks pale and shaken. “Mum?” I ask.
entries.translation: Onekaga arĩ mũmaku na akĩinaina. "Mami?" Ngĩĩtana.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)
Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: “Mum, what’s wrong?” She takes a deep breath and turns to face me.
entries.translation: "Mami, nĩ kĩĩ kĩũru?" Akĩhuhia na hinya na akĩĩhũgũra na akĩndora.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Her eyes are wide and filled with fear.
entries.translation: Maitho make marĩ marĩĩ na maihũirwo nĩ guoya.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)
Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: I follow her gaze out the window.

entries.english: At first, I don’t see anything.
entries.translation: Rĩa mbere, ndirona kĩndũ ona kĩ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: But then, I notice a movement in the shadows.
entries.translation: No thutha-inĩ, ngĩona kĩndũ kĩrathiĩ thĩini wa cĩĩruru.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: It’s a large, dark shape, and it’s moving towards the house.
entries.translation: Nĩ kĩndũ kĩnene, kĩirũ, na kĩrathiĩ gĩukite mwena wa nyũmba.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: “What is it?” I ask. “I don’t know,” Mum says. “But I don’t think it’s friendly.”
entries.translation: "Nĩ kĩĩ kĩu?" Ngĩũria. "Nĩĩ ndiũĩ," Mami akiuga. "No ndirona kaĩ kĩrĩ na ũrata."
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)
Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: It’s tall and slender, with long, spindly legs.
entries.translation: Nĩ kĩraihu na gĩceke, kĩrĩ na magũrũ maraya, mahĩnju.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Its body is covered in black fur, and its head is a smooth, round ball.
entries.translation: Mwĩrĩ wakĩo ũrĩ na guoya mũirũ, na mũtwe wakĩo nĩ muororo, wa gĩthiũrũri ta mũbira.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: It has no eyes, but I can see two large, pointed ears.
entries.translation: Gĩtirĩ na maitho, no nĩndĩrona matũ merĩ manene, maumĩru.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: “What are we going to do?” I ask.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: “We need to get out of here,” Mum says. “Now.”
entries.translation: "Twagĩrĩirwo nĩ kuuma haha," Mami akiuga. "Thaa ici."
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: We run out of the kitchen and into the living room.
entries.translation: Tũgĩteng'era tuumĩte riko na tũgĩthiĩ nyũmba nene.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)
Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Dad looks up from the TV. “What is it?” he asks.
entries.translation: Baba akĩhũgũka kuuma TV-inĩ. "Nĩ kĩĩ?" akĩũria.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: “I don’t know,” Mum says. “But it’s big and it’s coming this way.”
entries.translation: "Nĩĩ ndiũĩ nĩkĩ," Mami agĩcokia. "No nĩ kĩndũ kĩnene na kĩroka mwena ũyũ."
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Dad gets up from the couch.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: “We need to get out of here,” he says.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: We all run for the front door.
entries.translation: Ithuothe tũgĩteng'erera mũrango wa mwena wa mbere.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Mum unlocks it and we rush outside.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The creature is right behind us.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: It’s so close I can feel its hot breath on the back of my neck.
entries.translation: Nĩ gĩatũkuhĩrĩirie mũno nginya nĩndaiguaga mĩhũmũ yakio mĩhiũ thutha wa ngingo yakwa.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: We run to the car and get in.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Dad starts the engine and we peel out of the driveway.
entries.translation: Baba akĩrurumia ngari na tũkiumĩra ihenya gabara-inĩ ka muciĩ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The creature chases after us, but we’re too fast.
entries.translation: Kindũ kĩu gĩgĩtweng'eria, na nĩ twarĩ na ihenya mũno.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Movies have long been a powerful force in shaping our culture and our values.
entries.translation: Thenema nĩ ikoretwo irĩ hinya mũnene harĩ gũthondeka ũndũire witũ na mĩtugo iitũ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: They can influence our beliefs about everything from love and romance to war and violence.
entries.translation: No cihutie wĩtĩkio witũ wĩgiĩ maũndũ mothe kuuma kũrĩ wendo na wendani nginya mbaara na ngũĩ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: And they have a particularly strong influence on our ideas about gender roles.
entries.translation: Na nĩ cikoragwo na ũgucania mũnene na wa mwanya harĩ meciria maitũ megiĩ mawira ma arũme na atumia.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: For decades, Hollywood has perpetuated the stereotype of the ideal wife as a beautiful, submissive, and domestic woman who puts her husband and children first.
entries.translation: Kwa mĩaka mĩingĩ, kambuni ya Hollywood nĩ yonanĩtie atĩ mũtumia ũrĩa wagĩrĩire nĩ mũthaka, mwathĩki, na nĩ wa mũciĩ na nĩ aigaga mũrũme na ciana mbere.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: This image is often reinforced by the way that female characters are portrayed in movies.
entries.translation: Mbica ĩyo kaingĩ ĩheyagwo hinya nĩ ũrĩa athaki a thenema atumia monanagio thenema-inĩ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The majority of female characters were portrayed as either romantic interests or mothers.
entries.translation: Aingi aa athaki atumia monanagio ta arĩa marĩ na matanya ma kĩwendo kana atumia aciari.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: This narrow representation of women in film sends a powerful message to viewers about what it means to be a woman.
entries.translation: Wonania ũyũ mũkunderu wa atumia thĩĩni wa thenema nĩ ũtũmaga ndũmĩrĩri ndikĩru kũri eroreri ĩgiĩ ũria mũtumia atarii.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: It suggests that women's primary role is to be attractive and nurturing, and that their success is measured by their relationships with men and children.
entries.translation: Yonanagia atĩ wĩra wa mũthingi wa atumia nĩ kũgucĩrĩria na kũrera, na atĩ ũgacĩru wao ũthimagwo kũringana na ũrĩa marakuruhana na arũme na ciana.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: This idealized image of the wife can be harmful to women in several ways.
entries.translation: Mbica ĩno ya gwĩcirĩria ya mũtumia no ĩkorwo ĩrĩ na ũgwati kũrĩ atumia na njĩra nyingĩ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Patient: Doctor, I've been having this terrible stomach pain for the past few days.
entries.translation: Mũrwaru: Ndagĩtarĩ, ngoretwo ndĩ na ruo rũĩngi mũno rwa nda gwa thikũ cigana ũna hĩtũku.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: It's so bad that I can't eat or sleep.
entries.translation: Nĩ rũĩngĩ mũno atĩ ndĩngĩhota kũrĩa kana gũkoma.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: It's a sharp, stabbing pain that comes and goes.
entries.translation: Nĩ ruo rũnene, ta rwa gũthecwo rũria rũkaga rũgĩtigaga.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Doctor: Can you tell me more about the pain? Where is it located?
entries.translation: Ndagĩtarĩ: Hihi no ũhe ũhũro ũngi wĩgiĩ ruo rũu? Hihi ũrarũigwĩra ha?
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Patient: It's mostly in my lower abdomen, right around my belly button, but it sometimes radiates to my back.
entries.translation: Mũrwaru: Mũno mũno rwĩ mwena wa nda ya thĩĩ, hakuhĩ na mũkonyo, no rĩmwe nĩ rũthamagĩra mũgongo.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Doctor: Does anything make the pain worse?
entries.translation: Ndagĩtarĩ: Hihi gwĩ kĩndũ gĩtũmaga ruo rũu rwĩhe?
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Patient: Eating seems to make it worse, especially fatty or greasy foods.
entries.translation: Mũrwaru: rĩmwe kũrĩa nĩ gũtũmaga rwĩhe, makĩrĩa irio irĩ na maguta maingĩ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Doctor: And does anything make it better.?
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Patient: Lying down seems to help a little.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Doctor: Does the pain come and go, or is it constant?
entries.translation: Ndagĩtarĩ: Hihi ruo rũkaga rũgĩtigaga, kana nĩ rwa kĩrũmanĩrĩrio?
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Patient: It's constant. It's just a dull ache, but it's really uncomfortable.
entries.translation: Mũrwaru: Nĩ rwa kĩrũmanĩrĩrio. No gũturwo tu, no ningĩ nĩ kũrĩ ruo rũnene.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Doctor: Have you had any other symptoms? Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea?
entries.translation: Ndagĩtarĩ: Hihi wĩ na ndariri ĩngĩ? Kũira ngoro, gũtahĩka, kũharwo?
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)
Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Doctor: I see. Well, it sounds like you're having a case of gastritis.
entries.translation: Ndagĩtarĩ: Nĩndanyita. Nĩ kuuga, ũroneka nĩ ta wĩ na mũrimũ wa gastritis.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Gastritis is inflammation of the stomach lining.
entries.translation: Mũrimũ wa gastritis nĩ kũimba kwa rũthingo rwa nda.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: It can be caused by a number of things, including eating spicy or fatty foods, drinking alcohol, or taking certain medications.
entries.translation: Ũrehagwo nĩ maũndũ maĩngĩ, hamwe na kũrĩa irio ciĩ na icunjĩ cia kuongerera cama kana irĩ na maguta, kũnyua njohi, kana kũhũthĩra ndawa imwe.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)
Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Doctor: It can be, but in most cases it's not.
entries.translation: Ndagĩtarĩ: No ũkorwo, no kaingĩ ti mũũru.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: I'm going to prescribe you some medication to help relieve the pain and inflammation.
entries.translation: Nĩngũgũathĩra ndawa imwe cia gũgũteithia harĩ kũnina ruo na kũimba kũu.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: You should also avoid eating spicy or fatty foods, and drink plenty of fluids.
entries.translation: Nĩ wagĩrĩirwo gwĩthema kũria irio irĩ na maguta na icunji cia ũrugi, na ũnyue maai maingi.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: 1. Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease and flour an 8-inch round cake pan.
entries.translation: 1. Hiũhia riko nginya mwaki wa 350 F (ndigirii175 C). Haka rũgĩo rwa gĩthĩũrũrĩ rwa inji-8 mũtu.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: 2. In a medium bowl, whisk together the flours, granulated sugar, brown sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt.
entries.translation: 2. Tukania mĩtu yothe, cukari wa tũhiga, cukari wa gĩtĩri, ndawa ya kũimbia, igata rĩa kũruga, na cumbi thĩĩni wa mbakũri.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: 3. In a large bowl, cream together the butter and egg until light and fluffy. Beat in the egg yolk and almond extract.
entries.translation: 3. Tukania thĩagĩ na itumbĩ nginya ĩnyitane na ĩhuthe thĩĩni wa mbakũri nene. Ongerera mũruru wa itumbĩ na mũtutu wa mũrothi.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: 4. Gradually add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients, alternating with the milk. Mix until just combined.
entries.translation: 4. Ongerera o kahora indo nyũmũ nĩguo kũhehia iria ingĩ, ũgĩcenjanagia na iriya. Tukania nginya ĩtukane.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: 5. Fold in the almond flour until evenly distributed.
entries.translation: 5. Ongerera mũtu wa mũrothi nginya wũingĩre guothe.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: It was a hot summer day in July when I finally turned 16 years old.
entries.translation: Warĩ mũthenya wĩ na riũa mweri-inĩ wa Mũgwanja rĩrĩa ndakinyirie mĩaka 16.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: I had been eagerly anticipating this day for as long as I could remember, and now that it was finally here, I couldn't wait to get started on my road to freedom.
entries.translation: Nĩndetereire na kinyi mũthenya ũyũ kwa ihinda iraya ũrĩa ingĩririkana, na rĩu tondu mũthenya nĩ wakinya, ndingĩetereire rĩngĩ kwambia mũtũrĩre wa kwĩyatha.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The first step was to take the written test.
entries.translation: Ikinya rĩa mbere rĩarĩ gwĩka kĩgeranio gĩa kwandika.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: I studied hard for weeks, and I was confident that I would pass.
entries.translation: Ndathomire na kĩyo ciumia nyingĩ, na ndarĩ na mwĩhoko atĩ nĩ ngũhĩtũka.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: On the day of the test, I arrived at the DMV early and took my seat in the waiting room.
entries.translation: Mũthenya wa kĩgeranio, nĩndakinyire DMV tene na ngĩyoera gĩtĩ thĩĩni wa rumu ya gweterera.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: After a few hours, my name was called, and I was ushered into a small room with a computer.
entries.translation: Thutha wa mathaa manini, rĩtwa rĩakwa rĩgĩtwo, na ngĩtwarwo thĩĩni wa kanyumba kanini karĩ na kambiuta.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The test was surprisingly easy, and I finished it in no time.
entries.translation: Kĩgeranio kĩu kĩarĩ kĩhũthu mũno, na nĩndarĩkirie na ihenya.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: A few days later, I received a letter in the mail informing me that I had passed the written test.
entries.translation: Thutha wa thiku nini, nĩndatũmĩirwo marua makĩmenyithia atĩ nĩndahĩtũkĩte kĩgeranio kĩu.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The next step was to schedule a driving test.
entries.translation: Ikinya rĩu rĩngĩ rĩarĩ gũbanga kĩgeranio kĩa ũtereba.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: I called the DMV and made an appointment for the following week.
entries.translation: Ngĩhũra thimũ wabici-ini ya DMV na ngĩbanga mũthenya wa gũthiĩ kiumia kĩrĩa kĩarũmĩrĩire.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The day of my driving test arrived, and I was more nervous than I had ever been in my life.
entries.translation: Mũthenya wa kĩgeranio kĩa ũtereba ũgĩkinya, na ndirĩ ndaigua guoya ta ũcio ũtũũro-inĩ wakwa wothe.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: I drove to the DMV with my mom, who would be accompanying me on the test.
entries.translation: Twathire na mami wabici-inĩ ya DMV, ũrĩa ũngĩandwarire thiĩ ngeke kĩgeranio.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: "Heartbreak," sighed the poet, "is the cruelest of afflictions.
entries.translation: "Gũtuurio ngoro," mũtũngi ũcio wa marebeta agĩikĩria, "nĩ ũndũ wa kĩeha kĩũru.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: It is a pain that pierces the soul and leaves us feeling empty and alone.
entries.translation: Nĩ ruo rũrĩa rũthecaga ngoro na rũgatũtiga tĩkĩigwa ta tũrĩ a tũhũ na tũri wiki.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: It is a fire that burns from within, consuming us with its flames.
entries.translation: Nĩ mwaki ũrĩa ũcinaga kuuma thĩĩni, ũgatũnina na nĩnĩmbĩ cia guo.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: It is a storm that tears us apart, leaving us broken and scarred.
entries.translation: Nĩ rũhuho rũrĩa rũtũtarũraga, rũgatũtiga tuunĩkangĩkĩte na tũri na irema.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: But even in the midst of our heartbreak, there is hope.
entries.translation: No ũna gatagatĩ-inĩ ga gũturio ngoro gwitũ, kwĩna mwĩhoko.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: For even as our hearts are broken, they are also made new.
entries.translation: Tondũ o ta ũrĩa ngoro ciitũ ithũkangĩte, o nacio nĩ cierũhagio.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: We are given the opportunity to learn from our mistakes and to grow stronger.
entries.translation: Nĩ tũheyagwo kanya ga kwĩruta kuumana na mahĩtia maitũ na kũgĩa hinya makĩrĩa.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: We are given the chance to find love again, even if it is different than the love we have lost.
entries.translation: Nĩ tũheyagwo kanya ga gwetha wendo rĩngĩ, ona akorwo nĩ ngurani na uria urĩte.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: So let us not despair in our heartbreak.
entries.translation: Kũoguo rekei tũtigakue ngoro rĩrĩa twaturio ngoro.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Let us instead embrace it as a part of life.
entries.translation: Handu ha ũgũo, rekei tũũhĩmbĩrie ta ũndũ wa mũtũrĩre.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Let us learn from it and grow from it.
entries.translation: Rekei tũkũre na twĩrute na gũtũũrio ngoro.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: And let us never give up on the hope of finding love again"
entries.translation: Ona rĩ rekei tũtikanateyanĩrie mwĩhoko wa kuona wendo rĩngĩ"
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Judaism and Kosher Kosher is a set of dietary laws in Judaism.
entries.translation: Judaism na Kosher Kosher nĩ mũbango wa mawatho ma ũrĩĩ thĩĩni wa ndini ya Kĩyahundi.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: These laws define which foods are permissible to eat and which are not.
entries.translation: Mawatho maya mataragĩria ĩrĩo iria njĩtĩkĩrie kũrĩyo na ĩrĩa ngananie.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Kosher foods are those that are considered to be fit for consumption according to Jewish law.
entries.translation: Irio cia Kosher nĩ ĩrĩo ĩrĩa cionagwo ĩrĩ njagĩrĩru cia kũria kũringana na watho wa Kiyahundi.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The laws of kosher are based on the Torah, the first five books of the Hebrew Bible.
entries.translation: Mawatho ma Kosher maumĩte thĩĩni wa Torah, mabuku matano ma mbere thĩĩni wa Bibilia ya Kĩhibirania.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: These laws prohibit the consumption of certain animals, such as pigs and shellfish, as well as the consumption of blood and meat from animals that have not been slaughtered in a specific way.
entries.translation: Mawatho maya nĩ magirĩtie kũrĩa nyamũ itigaine, ta nguruwe na thamaki iria itarĩ ngũũci, ũndũ ũmwe na ũrĩĩ wa thakame na nyama ciumanĩte na nyamu itathĩnjĩtwo na njĩra ĩmwe.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Kosher foods are also subject to a number of other regulations, such as the separation of dairy and meat products.
entries.translation: Nĩngĩ ĩrĩo cia Kosher nĩcikoragwo na mawatho mangĩ maingĩ, ta gũtigĩthũkania indo ciumanĩte na iriya na cia nyama.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Kosher food is prepared in a way that ensures that it is fit for consumption according to Jewish law.
entries.translation: Irio cia Kosher ithondekagwo na njĩra ĩrĩa ĩratigĩrĩra atĩ nĩ njagĩrĩru cia kũrĩyo kũringana na watho wa Kĩyahundi.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: His work is also known for its influence on the philosophy of science.

entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Einstein is best known in popular culture for his mass–energy equivalence formula E = mc2 (which has been dubbed "the world's most famous equation").
entries.translation: Einstein ũĩkaine mũno nĩ ũndũ wa formula yake ya ũigananu wa ũritũ-hinya ya E = mc2 (iria yũĩkaine ta "ithabu rĩrĩa riũĩkaine mũno thĩĩni wa thĩĩ").
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Einstein was born in Ulm, in the Kingdom of Württemberg, German Empire, on 14 March 1879.
entries.translation: Einstein acĩarĩirwo Ulm, thĩĩni wa Ũthamaki wa Württemberg, Ũthamaki-inĩ mũnene wa Njerumani, tareki 14 mweri wa Gatatũ 1879.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: He showed an early aptitude for mathematics and physics.
entries.translation: Nĩ onanirie ũhoti wa kĩmerera wa mathabu na physics.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: In 1905, at the age of 26, Einstein published four groundbreaking papers that transformed physics.
entries.translation: Mwaka-inĩ wa 1905, arĩ na miaka 26, Einsten nĩ acabithirie maratathi mana ma mwanya marĩa macenjirie pysics.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Einstein's work led to a new understanding of the universe, and had a profound impact on the development of modern physics.
entries.translation: Wĩra wa Einstein nĩ warehire gũtaũkĩrwo kwerũ kwĩĩgiĩ thĩĩ, na nĩ wahutirie na njĩra nene mũno ũkũria wa sayansi ya kĩĩrĩu.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: He received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1921 for his explanation of the photoelectric effect.
entries.translation: Nĩ amũkĩrire ngerenwa ya Nobel thĩĩni wa Pysics mwaka-inĩ wa 1921 nĩ ũndũ wa gũtarĩrĩa maumĩrĩra ma photoelectric.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Einstein was a pacifist and a strong advocate for social justice.
entries.translation: Einstein arĩ mwendi thayu na mũrũĩrĩri wa ihoto cia ũmũndũ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Many people wake up before sunrise to start their day's work.
entries.translation: Andũ aingĩ mokĩraga riũa rĩtaumĩrĩte nĩguo manjie mawira mao ma mũthenya.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Farmers may rise before dawn to milk their cows or tend to their crops.
entries.translation: Arĩmi no mokire kĩroko tene nĩguo makame ng'ombe ciao kana magatungate ĩrĩo ciao.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Fishermen may go out to sea before the sun comes up.
entries.translation: Mũtegi wa thamaki no athie iriya-inĩ kaira riũya rĩrathĩte.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: People who work in the city may also wake up early to catch the bus or train to work.
entries.translation: Andu arĩa marutaga wĩra taũni onao nĩ mokagĩra tene nĩguo makore mbathi kana mũgithi wa gũthĩĩ wĩra.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Once people are up, they typically eat a simple breakfast of porridge, bread, or tea.
entries.translation: Rĩrĩa andũ mokĩra, kaingĩ mariyaga ĩrĩo hũthũ cia rũci-inĩ ta ũcũrũ, mũgate kana cai.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Then they get ready for the day.
entries.translation: Thutha ũcio makeharĩrĩa nĩ ũndũ wa mũthenya.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Many people in The Gambia wear traditional clothing, such as long dresses or skirts for women and long pants or shirts for men.
entries.translation: Andũ aingi bũrũri-inĩ wa Gambia mekagĩra nguo cia ũndũire, ta nguo ndaihu kana thikati cia atumia na mĩbuto mĩraihu kana cati cia arume.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: They may also wear a headscarf or cap.
entries.translation: Nĩngĩ no mekĩre ngũbia kana gitambaya kĩa mũtwe.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: After breakfast, people go about their daily activities.
entries.translation: Thutha wa irio cia rũci-inĩ, andũ marutaga mawĩra mao ma o mũthenya.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Children go to school, while adults go to work.
entries.translation: Ciana ithiyaga thukuru, na andũ agima magathiĩ wĩra.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Many people in The Gambia work in agriculture, fishing, or tourism.
entries.translation: Andũ aingĩ aa Gambia marutaga wĩra wa ũrĩmi, ũtegi wa thamaki, kana ũgendi.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Others work in government, business, or education.
entries.translation: Angĩ mararutaga wĩra wa thirikari, biacara, na gĩthimo.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: In the afternoon, people may take a break from work to relax or socialize.
entries.translation: Mĩaraho-inĩ, andũ nĩmaumaga wĩra-inĩ kwa ihinda nĩguo kũhuruka kana gũkuruhana.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: They may go for a walk, visit friends and family, or play games.
entries.translation: No mathie maumagare na magũrũ, macerere arata kana bamĩrĩ kana mathake.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: In the evening, people often eat dinner with their families.
entries.translation: Hwai-inĩ, kaingĩ andũ acio mariyaga irio hamwe na bamĩrĩ ciao.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Dinner is typically a simple meal of rice, vegetables, and meat or fish.
entries.translation: Irio cia ũtukũ nĩ hamwe na mũcere, mboga, na nyama kana thamaki.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The gadgets and utensils of the kitchen are a language, a means of communication between cook and food.
entries.translation: Indo cia kũruga thĩĩni wa riko nĩ ta rũthiomi, njĩra ya kwaranĩria gatagati ka mũrugi na irio.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The whisk, the tongs, the ladle, the spatula - each has its own meaning, its own purpose.
entries.translation: Kanyamũ ga kũhũra matumbĩ, gĩciko gĩa thubu, gĩciko - oo kimwe nĩ kĩrĩ uuge wakio, na wĩra wakio.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: To use them well is to understand the language of cooking, to season the dish with the flavors of experience and skill.
entries.translation: Gũcihũthĩra wega nĩ gũtaũkĩrwo rũthiomi rwa kũruga, kũruga irio ĩrĩ na mĩcamo ya ũmenyeru na ũhigĩriru.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The whisk is a whisk, the tongs are tongs, and the ladle is a ladle.
entries.translation: Kanyamu ga kũhũra matumbĩ, ga kũnyita makara ma mwaki, na gĩciko gĩa thubu ciothe nĩ ngũrani.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: But in the hands of a skilled cook, they become something more: they become extensions of the cook's own body, tools that allow him or her to express creativity and passion.
entries.translation: No moko-inĩ ma mũrugi wĩna ũhũgĩrĩru, indo icio ituĩkaga kindũ kĩngĩ: ituĩkaga ta ciĩga nyongerere mwiri-inĩ wa mũrugi, indo iria imũhotithagia kuonania ũũmbi na wendo.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: With a whisk, the cook can whip up a frothy batter or emulsify a delicate sauce.
entries.translation: Arĩ na kanyamũ ga kũhũra matumbi, mũrugi no athondeke thiagĩ njega kana aruge thubu mũmatu.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: With tongs, he or she can flip a steak or turn a roast.
entries.translation: Arĩ na tũcuma twa kũnyita mwaki, we no ahote kũgarũra gitũngũ kĩa nyama kana agarũre njino.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: With a ladle, he or she can ladle out a steaming bowl of soup or sauce.
entries.translation: Arĩ na gĩciko gĩa thubu, we no ahote gũtahia mbakũri ya thubu mũhiu mũno.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The gadgets and utensils of the kitchen are more than just tools.
entries.translation: Indo cia riko na indo cia kũruga nĩ makĩria ya indo cia wĩra.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: They are a means of expression, a way to create something beautiful and delicious.
entries.translation: Nĩ njĩra ya kwĩyonania, na njĩra gũthondeka kindũ gĩthaka na kĩrĩ na cama.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: A seed is a small, dormant plant embryo that is capable of developing into a new plant under the right conditions.
entries.translation: Mbegũ nĩ kongero kanini, gatararuta wĩra karĩa karĩ na ũhoti wa gũkũra na gũtuika mũmera mwerũ kũgerera maũndũ marĩa magĩrĩire.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: When a seed sprouts, it begins to grow roots and shoots.
entries.translation: Rĩrĩa mbegũ yamera, nĩ yanjagia gũkũra mĩrĩ na kuumĩra.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The roots anchor the plant in the soil and absorb water and nutrients from the ground.
entries.translation: Mĩrĩ ĩnyitagĩrĩra mũmera thĩĩni wa tĩri-inĩ na kũgucia maĩ na ĩrĩo kuuma tĩri-inĩ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The shoots grow upwards towards the sun, and the leaves begin to photosynthesize, producing food for the plant.
entries.translation: Kahuti kau gakũraga na igũrũ kerekeire riũa, na mahuti makanjia gũthondeka ũtheri, nĩguo kũrutĩra mũmera ũcio irio.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: As the plant grows, it develops a stem, leaves, flowers, and fruit.
entries.translation: Oo mũmera ũgĩkũraga, ũkũragia mũti, mathangũ, mahũa, na matunda.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The flowers produce seeds, which are dispersed by wind, water, or animals.
entries.translation: Mahũa marũtaga mbegũ, ĩrĩa ĩhurunjagwo nĩ rũhuho, maĩ, kana nyamũ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: When a seed lands in a suitable location, it can germinate and begin the process of growth all over again.
entries.translation: Rĩrĩa mbegũ yagwa handũ harĩa hagĩrĩire, no ĩmere na yanjie mũtaratara wa gũkũra o rĩngĩ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The process of seed germination is a marvel of nature.
entries.translation: Kũmera kwa mbegũ nĩ ũndũ wa magegania wa kĩmerera.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: It is a testament to the power of life and the resilience of the natural world.
entries.translation: Nĩ ũira wa kuonania hinya wa muoyo na ucamba wa thĩĩ ya ndũire.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: When a seed sprouts, it is a sign of hope and new beginnings.
entries.translation: Rĩrĩa mbegũ yamera, nĩ kĩonereria kĩa mwĩhoko na ciambĩrĩria njerũ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: We hope that this ban will serve as a warning to others who may be tempted to engage in similar behavior.

entries.english: We will not tolerate this type of behavior on our forum, and we will take action to protect our community from it.

Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: "I'm telling you, I used my turn signal!"

Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: "At least I know how to drive!"

entries.translation: "Haiya, nĩguo? Ndĩ mwandĩki mwega makĩria gũgũkĩra!"

Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.translation: "Ti ũndũ wa kwarĩrĩria! Ndĩ Ernest Hemingway!"
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)
Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: "Ernest Hemingway! The greatest writer of all time!"
entries.translation: "Ernest Hemingway! Mwandĩki ũrĩa mwega biu wa mahinda mothe!"
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Grace: Can you tell me a little bit about its history?
entries.translation: Grace: Hihi no ũnjĩre maũndũ manini megiĩ kĩhumo gĩa cai?
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Teacher: Of course. Tea originated in China, where it has been cultivated for over 5,000 years.
entries.translation: Mũrutani: Hatarĩ nganja. Kĩhumo gĩa cai nĩ kũrĩa Caina, kũrĩa ũkoretwo ũkĩrĩmwo kwa makĩria ma mĩaka 5,000.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The first written record of tea dates back to the 3rd century BC, when it was mentioned in a Chinese medical text.
entries.translation: Ũhoro wa mbere wa cai wandĩkirwo karine ya 3 mbere ya Kristo, rĩrĩa wagwetĩrwo ibuku-inĩ rĩa ũrigitani rĩa Caina.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Tea was originally used as a medicinal herb, but it quickly became a popular drink among Chinese people of all social classes.
entries.translation: Cai wahũthagĩrwo ta ihuti rĩa ũrigiti, no nĩwatũikire kinywanji kĩrĩ ngumo na ihenya kũrĩ andũ a Caina kuuma mĩhĩrĩga yothe ya mũtũrĩre.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Grace: What about outside of China? When did tea start to spread to other parts of the world?
entries.translation: Grace: Ĩĩ hihi nja wa Caina? Cai wanjirie gũtamba nginya icigo ingĩ cia thĩĩ rĩ?
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Teacher: Tea was first introduced to Europe in the 16th century by Portuguese traders.
entries.translation: Mũrutani: Cai waingĩrĩirio rĩa mbere mwena wa Rũraya karine-inĩ ya 16 nĩ ahũri biacara a Portugal.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: It quickly became popular among European elites, and by the 18th century, tea had become a staple of British culture.
entries.translation: Nĩwagĩire ngumo na ihenya kũri atongoria a Rũraya, na gũgĩkinya karine ya 18, nĩwatũikire kĩndũ gĩa bata ũndũire-inĩ wa Ngeretha.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: In the 19th century, tea was also introduced to North America, where it became a popular drink among both colonists and Native Americans.
entries.translation: Karine-inĩ ya 19, cai nĩwatwarirwo mwena wa Amerika ya Rũgongo, kũrĩa watuĩkire kĩnywaji kĩ ngumo kũrĩ akoroni na Aturi a tene a Amerika.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Grace: That's really interesting.I never knew that tea had such a long history.
entries.translation: Grace: ũcio ni ũndũ wa magegania mũno. Ndiroĩ cai nĩ ũrĩ historĩ ndaihu ũgũo.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Teacher: It's a fascinating story, and it's one that's still being written today.
entries.translation: Mwarimũ: Nĩ rũgano rwa magegania, na no rũrathiĩ na mbere kwandĩkwo ũmũthi.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: During World War II, the Allies and Axis powers used a variety of aircraft to achieve air superiority.
entries.translation: Hindĩ ya mbara ya Kerĩ ya thĩĩ, mĩena ya Allies na Axis nĩ yahũthagĩra mĩthemba ngũrani ya ndege nĩguo gũtũgĩra rĩera-inĩ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: One of the most important factors in determining the outcome of a battle was the accuracy of the aircraft's bombing.
entries.translation: Kĩndũ gĩa bata mũno harĩ gũthima maũmĩrĩra ma mbara kĩarĩ ũhoti wa ndege ĩyo gũthimĩrĩria rĩrĩa ĩrarekia mbomu.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The height at which an aircraft could fly was also a critical factor, as it determined how far it could travel and how much weight it could carry.
entries.translation: Ũraihu ũria ndege ĩngĩombũkire warĩ kĩndu gĩa bata mũno, tondũ nĩguo watũmaga mamenye ĩngĩthie nginya ha na ũritũ ũrĩa ĩngĩhota gũkua.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The United States developed a number of high-altitude bombers during the war, including the B-17 Flying Fortress and the B-29 Superfortress.
entries.translation: Bũrũri wa Amerika nĩwathondekire ndege cia kũrekia mbomu kuuma ũraihu mũnene hindĩ ya mbara, hamwe na B-17 Flying Fortress na B-29 Superfortress.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: These aircraft were able to fly at altitudes of over 30,000 feet, which made them difficult for enemy fighters to intercept.
entries.translation: Ndege ici ciarĩ na ũhoti wa kũũmbũka makĩrĩa ma ũraihu wa fiti 30,000, ũndũ ũrĩa watumaga arũi a thũũ maremwo gũcihĩta.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: They also carried a large payload of bombs, which could be used to attack targets deep behind enemy lines.
entries.translation: Ningĩ nĩciakuwaga mbomu cia ũritũ mũingĩ, iria cingĩahũthĩrirwo gũtharĩkĩra thũũ ona rĩrĩa ciĩhithite mwena wacio.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The German Luftwaffe also developed a number of high-altitude bombers, including the Heinkel He 177 Greif and the Messerschmitt Me 264 Amerika Bomber.
entries.translation: Athondeki a German Luftwaffe nĩmathondekire ndege cia kurekia mbomu kuuma ũraihu mũnene, hamwe na Heinkel He 177 na Messerschmitt Me 264 Amerika Bomber.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: These aircraft were not as successful as their American counterparts, however, due to a number of technical problems.
entries.translation: Ona kũrĩ ũguo, ndege ici citiarĩ na ũgaciru ta iria cia aruna ao a Amerika, nĩ ũndũ wa mathina kahiri ma kĩmũtambo na ũthondeki.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: I know what you did yesterday.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: You posted a picture of yourself wearing that green rag on social media.
entries.translation: Nĩ ũratũmire mbica yaku wĩkĩrĩte gĩtambara kĩrĩa gĩaku kĩa rũnyaga rwa nyeni nenda-inĩ cia ũkinyanĩria.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: I know you thought it was funny, but it wasn’t.
entries.translation: Nĩ njũĩ wonire tarĩ ũndũ wa gũthekania, no ndwarĩ ũguo.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: It was disrespectful to your mother, and it hurt her feelings.
entries.translation: Ũndũ ũcio ndwarĩ wa gĩtĩyo harĩ mami wanyu, na nĩ waturirie ngoro yake.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: I’m not asking you to apologize because I’m mad at you.
entries.translation: Nĩndakwira ũcunge mũhera tondũ ningũrakarĩire mũno.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: I’m asking you to apologize because it’s the right thing to do.
entries.translation: Ndĩrakwĩra ũcunge mũhera tondũ ũcio nĩ ũndũ ũrĩa wagĩrĩire gwĩka.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Your mother loves you, and she deserves your respect.
entries.translation: Mami wanyu nĩ akwendete, na nĩ wagĩrĩire kũmũhe gĩtĩyo gĩaku.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Please call her today and tell her you’re sorry.
entries.translation: Ndakũhoya ũmũhũrĩre thimũ na ũmũcũnge mũhera.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Tell her that you didn’t mean to hurt her feelings, and that you promise to never wear that green rag again.
entries.translation: Ũmũĩre atĩ ndũrarĩ wendi waku kũmũtuuria ngoro, na ũmwĩrĩre atĩ ndũgekĩra gĩtambara kĩu kĩa rũnyaga rwa nyeni rĩngĩ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: I know you’re a good person, and I know you love your mother.
entries.translation: Nĩnjũĩ atĩ wĩ mũndũ mwega, na nĩnjũĩ atĩ nĩwendete mami wanyu.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: So please, do the right thing and apologize.
entries.translation: Kuoguo ndakũhoya, ĩka ũndũ ũrĩa wagĩrĩire na ũhoye mũhera.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: After you apologize to your mother, I want you to burn that green rag.
entries.translation: Thutha wa kũhoya mamiguo mũhera, ndĩrenda ũcine gĩtambara kĩu kĩa rũnyaga rwa nyeni.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: It’s a symbol of your disrespect, and it needs to be gone.
entries.translation: Nĩ kĩonereria gĩa kwaga gĩtĩyo, na kĩagĩrĩire gũteyo kaimana.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: I know it might be hard to let go of that rag, but it’s important.
entries.translation: Nĩnjũĩ no ũkorwo ũrĩ ũndũ mũritũ gũtee gĩtambara kĩu, no nĩ ũndũ wa bata.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: It’s a symbol of your past, and it’s time to move on.
entries.translation: Nĩ kĩonereria kĩa maica maku mahĩtũku, ihinda nĩ ikinyu rĩa gũthiĩ mbere.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)
Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)
Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: And you don’t need that rag to define you anymore.
entries.translation: Na ndũrabatara gĩtambara nĩguo gwĩtambũra rĩngĩ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)
Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Burn it and let it go.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: And then go hug your mother and tell her you love her.
entries.translation: Thutha ũcoke ũthie na ũhĩmbĩrie mami wanyu na ũmwire nĩ ũmwendete.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)
Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: A car was driving too fast and lost control, swerving into the other lane and hitting a car head-on.
entries.translation: Ngari yathiyaga ihenya mũno na ĩgĩte mwerekera, ĩkĩingira mwena ũria ũngi wa bara na ĩgĩturumana na ngari ĩngĩ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The driver of the first car was killed instantly, and the driver of the second car was seriously injured.
entries.translation: Ndereba wa ngari ya mbere akuire hau, nake ndereba wa ngari ya kerĩ akĩgurario ũũru.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: My friend Joseph called me to talk about it.
entries.translation: Mũrata wakwa Joseph akĩhũrĩra nĩguo twarie ũhoro ũcio.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: "It's so sad," he said. "I can't imagine how the families of the victims are coping."
entries.translation: "Nĩ ũndũ wa kĩeha mũno," akiuga. "Ndingĩenda gwĩcirĩria ũria bamĩrĩ cia arĩa monire mũtino iraigua."
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: "Me neither," I responded. "It's a reminder that we need to be careful when we're driving.
entries.translation: "O na niĩ," Ngĩcokia. "Nĩ kĩririkanio atĩ nĩtwagĩrĩire gũkorwo na ũbacirĩri rĩrĩa tũratwarithia ngari.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Even a small mistake can have devastating consequences."
entries.translation: Ona mahĩtia manini no makorwo na maumĩrĩra moru mũno."
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: "I agree," replied Jo. "We all need to follow the rules of the road and drive defensively."
entries.translation: "Nĩguo," Jo agĩcokia. "Ithuothe nĩ twagĩrĩirwo kũrũmĩrĩrra mawatho ma bara na gũtwarithia na ũgitĩri."
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: "Absolutely," I quickly added. "And we need to be aware of the dangers of distracted driving. Things like texting and talking on the phone can take our attention away from the road and lead to accidents."
entries.translation: "Nĩ ma," ngĩongerera na ihenya. "Na nĩtwagĩrĩirwo gũkorwo tũkimenya mogwati ma gũtwarithia ngari tũgikaga ũndũ ũngi. Maũndũ ta kũhũthĩra thimũ no matume twage kũrora bara na macũngĩrĩrie mĩtino."
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: "I know," said Jo sheepishly. "I'm guilty of it myself sometimes."
entries.translation: "Nĩ njui," Jo akiuga aconokete. "Nĩngoragwo na ũcuke wa ũndũ ũcio rĩmwe na rĩmwe."
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: In the small town of Malgudi, there was a corrupt police inspector named Ramasamy.
entries.translation: Thĩĩni wa taũni nini ya Malgudi, nĩ kwarĩ na mũnene wa borithi mungumania wetagwo Ramasamy.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: He would often take bribes from the people he arrested, and he would also use his power to harass and intimidate people.
entries.translation: Kaingĩ oyaga mahaki kuuma kũrĩ andũ arĩ aikia ngono, na nĩ angĩahũthĩrire hinya wake kũhinyĩrĩria andũ na kũmamakia.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: One day, Ramasamy arrested a young man named Krishnan for a crime he did not commit.
entries.translation: Mũthenya ũmwe, Ramasamy nĩ aikirie ngono mwanake ũgwĩtwo Krishman nĩ ũndũ wa ihĩtia atekĩte.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Krishnan was innocent, but Ramasamy refused to listen to him.
entries.translation: Krishman ndarĩ na ũcuke, no Ramasamy akĩrega kũmũthikĩrĩria.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: He demanded a bribe from Krishnan, and when Krishnan refused to pay, Ramasamy threw him in jail.
entries.translation: Etirie Krishman ihaki, na rĩrĩa Krishman aregire kũrĩha ihaki rĩu, Ramasamy akĩmwiikia njera.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Krishnan's father, a poor farmer, was desperate to get his son out of jail.
entries.translation: Baba wa Krishman, mũrĩmi mũthiini, nĩ eendaga mũno kũruta mũrũwe njera.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: He went to see Ramasamy and begged him to release Krishnan, but Ramasamy refused.
entries.translation: Nĩ athire kuonana na Ramasamy na akĩmũthaitha arekererie Krishman, no Ramasamy akĩrega.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The farmer then went to the local temple and prayed to God for help.
entries.translation: Mũrimĩ ũcio agĩcoka agĩthiĩ thĩĩni wa hekarũ ya itũũra na akĩhoya Ngai amũteithie.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The next day, the farmer was walking home from the temple when he saw a large snake crossing the road.
entries.translation: Mũthenya ũria warũmĩrĩire, mũrĩmi ũcio athiyaga mũciĩ aumĩte hekarũ-inĩ rĩrĩa onire nyoka nene ĩgĩkĩra barabara.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The farmer was afraid of snakes, but he knew that he had to do something to help his son.
entries.translation: Mũrĩmi ũcio nĩ etigagĩra nyoka, no nĩ amenyaga atĩ no nginya angĩekire ũndũ nĩguo ateithie mũrũwe.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: He picked up the snake and carried it to the police station.
entries.translation: Akĩoya nyoka ĩyo na akĩmĩkuwa o nginya ceceni-inĩ ya borithi.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: When Ramasamy saw the snake, he was terrified.
entries.translation: Rĩrĩa Ramasamy onire nyoka iyo, nĩ aiguire guoya mũno.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Dentist: Let me take a look. [Examines the patient's teeth.] Hmm, it looks like you have a cavity.
entries.translation: Ndagĩtarĩ wa Magego: Reke ndore. [Akĩrora magego ma mũrwaru.] Ũroneka, nĩ ta wenjekete igego.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: I'm going to need to drill out the decay and fill the hole.
entries.translation: Rĩu ngũruta hau igego rĩenjekete na thinge irima rĩu.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)
Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Dentist: It might be a little uncomfortable, but I'll do my best to make it as painless as possible.
entries.translation: Ndagĩtari wa Magego: Wahota kwaga kũigwa wega, no ningĩ nĩngwĩrutanĩria mũno nĩguo ndũkaigue ruo mũno.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Dentist: (gives the patient a local anesthetic) Okay, this will numb the area so you won't feel anything.
entries.translation: Ndagĩtarĩ wa Magego: (akahe mũrwaru ndawa ya kũgonia) Riu, ndawa ino nĩ igũkũgonia nĩguo ndũkaigwe kĩndũ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Dentist: (drills out the decay and fills the hole) All done!
entries.translation: Ndagĩtarĩ wa Magego: (akaruta kwenjeka na agathinga irima riũ) Nĩndarĩkia!
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Patient: Thank you, doctor. That wasn't so bad.
entries.translation: Mũrwaru: Nĩ ngatho, ndagĩtarĩ. Nduuma ũndũ mũru mũno.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Dentist: You're welcome. Just be sure to brush and floss regularly to prevent future cavities.
entries.translation: Ndagĩtarĩ wa Magego: Nĩ ngatho. Ririkanaga gwĩkinya magego na kũruta irio magego-inĩ kaingĩ nĩguo kũrigĩrĩria kwenjeka ringĩ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Patient: I will Dentist: (hands the patient a list of instructions) Here are some instructions on how to care for your new filling.
entries.translation: Mũrwaru: Ningwĩka ũguo Ndagĩtarĩ: (akanengera mũrwaru motaaro) Maya nĩ mootaro megiĩ ũmenyereri wa hau twathinga.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)
Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Dear [Name], I hope this letter finds you well.
entries.translation: Mwendwa [Rĩtwa], ngwĩhoka irũa rĩrĩ nĩrĩgũgũkinyĩra wega.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: I'm writing to you from our family farm, where the harvest has been going well this year.
entries.translation: Ndĩramwandĩkĩra ndĩ gũkũ mũgũnda-inĩ wa bamĩrĩ, kũrĩa igetha rĩrathiĩ na mbere wega mwaka-inĩ ũyũ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: We're expecting a bumper crop of sugarcane, which is used to make rum.
entries.translation: Nĩ tũrehoka nĩ tũkũgĩa na igetha inene rĩa igwa, iria tũkũhũthĩra gũthondeka njohi.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Rum is a distilled spirit made from sugarcane molasses or sugarcane juice.
entries.translation: Rum nĩ njohi ĩtweketio na thibiriti ĩthondeketwo kuumana cukari-inĩ wa igwa kana ngogoyo ya igwa.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: It's typically aged in wooden barrels, which gives it its characteristic flavor.
entries.translation: Kaingĩ ĩrugagĩrwo tũtangi-inĩ twa mbao, tũrĩa tũmĩheyaga mũcamo wayo wa mwanya.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Rum can be enjoyed neat, on the rocks, or mixed in cocktails.
