entries.english: We talked for a few minutes before the bell rang for class to start.
entries.translation: Twaririe dagĩka nini mbere ya ngengere kũrĩra nĩ getha gĩthomo kĩambĩrĩrie.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Ms. Smith began by introducing herself and telling us about the rules of the classroom.
entries.translation: Ms. Smith akĩambĩrĩria kwĩmenyithania kũrĩ ithuĩ na gũtwĩra ũhoro wa mawatho ma kĩrathi-inĩ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Then, she started teaching us about math.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: I was a little bit confused at first, but Ms. Smith explained everything clearly.
entries.translation: Nĩ datukanĩirũo hanini hau mbere-inĩ, no Ms. smith agĩtarĩria maũndũ mothe wega.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: After math class, we had a break.
entries.translation: Thuutha wa gĩthomo gĩa mathabu, tũgĩthĩ kũhurũka.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Sarah and I went outside to play on the playground.
entries.translation: Sarah na niĩ twathiire nja gũthaka kĩwanja-inĩ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: We played on the swings and the slide for a while, then we went back inside for lunch.
entries.translation: Twathakire icuho-inĩ na mũnyũrũrũ-inĩ gwa kahinda, tũgĩcoka tũkĩingĩra kũrĩa irio cia mũthenya.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: When tissue is injured, the body’s immune system sends white blood cells to the area.
entries.translation: Rĩrĩa kĩĩga kĩa mwĩrĩ gĩatihio, mũbango wa mwĩrĩ wa kũgitĩra mwĩrĩ nĩ ũtũmaga tũhengereta tũtheru twa thakame handũ hau.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: These cells release chemicals that cause blood vessels to dilate and become more permeable.
entries.translation: Tũhengereta tũũtũ tũrutaga kemiko iria itũmaga mĩcibi ya thakame kwarama na kũhota kũgereka makĩria.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: This allows fluid and white blood cells to leak out of the blood vessels and into the injured tissue.
entries.translation: Gũũkũ nĩ gũteithagia maaĩ na tũhengereta tũtheru twa thakame kuuma mĩcibi-inĩ ya thakame na kũingĩra kĩĩga-inĩ gĩtihie.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The fluid forms a clear, watery swelling called edema.
entries.translation: Maaĩ macio nĩ mathondekaga ũimbu mũtheru, ũhaana maaĩ wĩtagũo edema.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The white blood cells help to fight infection and to remove damaged tissue.
entries.translation: Tũhengereta tũu tũtheru twa thakame nĩ tũteithagia kũrũa mũrimũ na kũruta kĩĩga kĩrĩa gĩthũkangie.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: They also release chemicals that stimulate the growth of new tissue.
entries.translation: Ona ningĩ nĩ tũrutaga kemiko iria iteithagia na gũkũra kwa kĩĩga kĩerũ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The classic signs of acute inflammation are redness, heat, swelling, and pain.
entries.translation: Imenyithia nene cia kũrũara nĩ ũtune, ũrugarĩ, ũimbu, na ruo.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: These signs are caused by the increased blood flow and the release of chemicals in the injured tissue.
entries.translation: Imenyithia ici cirehagũo nĩ ũingĩrĩrĩku wa thakame na kũrutũo gwa kemiko thĩiniĩ wa kĩĩga kĩrĩa kĩrũaru.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Redness is caused by the dilation of blood vessels.
entries.translation: Ũtune ũrehagũo nĩ kwarama gwa mĩcibi ya thakame.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Heat is caused by the increased blood flow and the release of inflammatory chemicals.
entries.translation: Ũrugarĩ ũrehagũo nĩ ũingĩrĩrĩku wa thakame na kũrutũo gwa kemiko cia kũrũara.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Swelling is caused by the leakage of fluid from blood vessels into the injured tissue.
entries.translation: Ũimbu ũrehagũo nĩ gũitĩka gwa maaĩ kuuma mĩcibi ya thakame o nginyagia kĩĩga kĩrũaru.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Pain is caused by the release of inflammatory chemicals and the pressure of the swelling.
entries.translation: Ruo rũrehagũo nĩ kũrekererio gwa kemiko cia kũrũara na hatĩka ya kũimba.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Acute inflammation is a normal part of the healing process.
entries.translation: Kũrũara hanini nĩ mũtaratara wagĩrĩire wa ũhona.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: However, if it is severe or prolonged, it can damage healthy tissue.
entries.translation: Ona kũrĩ ũguo, angĩkorũo nĩ mũrimũ mũũru kana wa kahinda karaihu, no ũthũkie kĩĩga kĩega.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: In some cases, acute inflammation can lead to chronic inflammation, which is a long-term condition that can cause pain, disability, and even death.
entries.translation: Rĩmwe, kũrũara hanini no kũrehe mũrimũ wa gũtũũra, ũrĩa nĩ wa kahinda karaihu na ũrehe ruo, wathe, ona kana gĩkuũ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: There are a number of things that can cause acute inflammation, including infection, injury, and autoimmune diseases.
entries.translation: Nĩ kũrĩ maũndũ mamwe mangĩrehe mũrimũ mũnini, ta kũrũara, gũtihio, na mĩrimũ ya kũrehũo nĩ ũgitĩri wa mwĩrĩ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Infections are caused by bacteria, viruses, or fungi.
entries.translation: Mĩrimũ ĩrehagũo nĩ bacteria, virus, ona fungi.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: When these organisms enter the body, they can trigger an immune response that leads to inflammation.
entries.translation: Rĩrĩa indo ici cirĩ mũoyo cingĩraga mwĩrĩ-inĩ, no citũme kaũndũ ka ũgitĩri wa mwĩrĩ karĩa kangĩrehe kũrũara.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.translation: Gũtihangio ona kuo no kũrehe mũrimũ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: When tissue is damaged, it releases chemicals that attract white blood cells and other immune cells to the area.
entries.translation: Kĩĩga kĩarũara, nĩ kĩrutaga kemiko iria igucagĩrĩria tũherengeta tũtheru twa thakame na tũhengereta tũngĩ twa ũgitĩri wa thakame kũrĩ handũ hau.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: These cells release chemicals that cause inflammation.
entries.translation: Tũherengeta tũũtũ nĩ tũrutaka kemiko iria irehaga mũrimũ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Autoimmune diseases are caused by the body’s immune system attacking its own tissues.
entries.translation: Mĩrimũ ĩrĩa ĩrehagũo nĩ mũbango wa ũgitĩri wa mwĩrĩ ĩrehagũo nĩ ũndũ wa mũbango wa ũgitĩri wa mwĩrĩ kũhũrana na ciĩga ciaguo mwene.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: This can lead to inflammation in the affected tissues.
entries.translation: Gũũkũ no kũrehe mũrimũ thĩiniĩ wa ciĩga iria hutie.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Acute inflammation is usually treated with pain relievers, such as ibuprofen or acetaminophen.
entries.translation: Kũrũara hanini kũhonagio na dawa cia kũnina ruo, ta ibuprofen kana acetaminophen.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: In some cases, corticosteroids may be used to reduce inflammation.
entries.translation: Maita mangĩ, corticosteroids no ĩhũthiro kũnyihia mũrimũ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: If the inflammation is caused by an infection, antibiotics may be prescribed.
entries.translation: Angĩkorũo mũrimũ ũcio ũrehetũo nĩ kũrũara, dawa cia kũraga bacteria no ciheanũo.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Chronic inflammation is a long-term condition that can cause pain, disability, and even death.
entries.translation: Mũrimũ ũtarathira nĩ kaundũ ga kahinda karaihu karĩa kangĩrehe ruo, wathe, ona kana gĩkuũ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: It is often caused by autoimmune diseases, such as rheumatoid arthritis and Crohn’s disease.
entries.translation: Kaingĩ kũrehagũo nĩ mĩrimũ ĩrehegũo nĩ ũgitĩri wa mwĩrĩ, ta rheumatoid arthritis na mũrimũ wa Crohn.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Chronic inflammation can also be caused by obesity, smoking, and air pollution.
entries.translation: Mũrimũ ũtathiraga no ũrehũo nĩ ũritũ mũnene mũno wa mwĩrĩ, kũnyua thigara, na gũthũka kwa rĩera.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: There is no cure for chronic inflammation, but it can be managed with medication, lifestyle changes, and physical therapy.
entries.translation: Gũtirĩ kĩhonia kĩa mũrimũ ũtathiraga, no ningĩ no ũmenyererũo na dawa, gũcenjia mũikarĩre, na ũrigitani wa mwĩrĩ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The Mozambican Civil War was a conflict that lasted from 1977 to 1992.
entries.translation: Mbaara ya Raiya ya Mozambique yaarĩ mbaara yaikarire kuuma 1977 nginya 1992.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The war caused widespread devastation and displacement, and led to the deaths of an estimated 1 million people.
entries.translation: Mbaara ĩyo yarehire gũkua ngoro na gwĩthara kũnene, na gũkĩrehe ikuũ cia andũ ta mirioni 1.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The war began after RENAMO launched an insurgency against FRELIMO in 1977.
entries.translation: Mbaara ĩyo yambĩrĩirie thuutha wa RENAMO kwambia ũkararia wa FRELIMO mwaka wa 1977.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: RENAMO was opposed to FRELIMO's socialist policies and its close ties to the Soviet Union.
entries.translation: RENAMO nĩ yaregaga ũteti wa gĩsocialisti wa FRELIMO na ngwatanĩro ciayo cia hakuhĩ kũrĩ Soviet Union.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The war quickly escalated, and by the early 1980s, RENAMO had control of much of the countryside.
entries.translation: Mbara ĩyo nĩ yaingĩhire o rĩmwe, na kũrĩ mĩaka-inĩ ya mbere ya 1980, RENAMO nĩ yarĩ na hinya igũrũ ria gĩcagi kĩũ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: FRELIMO was forced to rely on Soviet and Cuban military aid to keep RENAMO at bay.
entries.translation: FRELIMO no mũhaka ĩngĩehokire ũteithio wa Soviet na Cuba wa kĩnjeci nĩ getha mahotane na RENAMO.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: In 1984, FRELIMO and RENAMO signed a peace agreement, but the fighting continued.
entries.translation: Kũrĩ 1984, FRELIMO na RENAMO nĩ ciekĩrire kĩrore ũiguano wa thayũ, na mbara nĩ yathire na mbere.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: In 1992, the two sides signed a new peace agreement, which called for a ceasefire and the holding of multiparty elections.
entries.translation: Kũrĩ 1992, mĩena ĩyo ĩĩrĩ nĩ yekĩrire kĩrore ũiguano wa thayũ, ũrĩa wetigithirie kũrũa na gwĩkithia ithurano cia ciama nyingĩ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: It was a bright and sunny day in the small village of Locksmiths, and the festival of locks was in full swing.
entries.translation: Kwarĩ mũthenya mũtheru na mwaru gatũũra-inĩ ga Locksmiths, na gĩathĩ gĩa iburi nĩ kĩambĩtie.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The streets were crowded with people, all eager to see the latest and greatest in lockmaking technology.
entries.translation: Barabara ciaiũire andũ, othe metereire kũona tekinoronjĩ njerũ na nene ya ũthondeki wa makuburi.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: There were vendors selling everything from simple padlocks to complex combination locks, and artisans demonstrating their skills in lockpicking and locksmithing.
entries.translation: Kwarĩ na endia mendagia indo ciothe kuma makuburi mahũthũ nginyagia makuburi ma mĩtũkanio mĩritũ, na jorua ikĩonania ũhoti wao wa kũbunja makuburi na gũtura makuburi.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: In the center of the village square, a large stage had been set up for the day's festivities.
entries.translation: Gatagatĩ-inĩ wa kĩhaaro gĩa itũũra, nĩ kwarĩ na mbere ya harĩrĩirio nĩ ũndũ wa ciathĩ cia mũthenya ũcio.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: A group of musicians were playing lively tunes, and a crowd of people were gathered around, clapping and dancing.
entries.translation: Gĩkundi kĩa aini nĩ mathakaga nyĩmbo njega, na gĩkundi kĩa andũ nĩ gĩathiũrũrũkĩte, makĩhũra hĩ na gũthũngũtha.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: On the stage, a skilled locksmith was demonstrating how to pick a lock, and the crowd was mesmerized by his skill.
entries.translation: Hau mbeere, mũthondeki jorua wa makuburi nĩ onanagia gũtua makuburi, na gĩkundi nĩ gĩakenirio nĩ ũũgĩ wake.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: As the sun began to set, the festival came to a close.
entries.translation: Rĩrĩa riũa rĩambĩrĩirie gũthũa rĩ, gĩathĩ gĩgĩthira.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: My friend, Abel, and I were walking home from school one day when we saw a blood drive being held at our local community center.
entries.translation: Mũrata wakwa, Abel, na niĩ twathiaga mũciĩ kuuma cukuru mũthenya ũmwe rĩrĩa tũonire ũheani wa thakame ũgĩkũo thoko-inĩ ya itũũra rĩtũ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: We were both 17 years old, and we had never donated blood before.
entries.translation: Ithuerĩ twarĩ na mĩaka 17, na tũtiarĩ tũheanĩte thakame rĩngĩ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: We decided to stop in and see what it was all about.
entries.translation: Tũgĩtua itua kũingĩra kuo na kũona nĩ kĩĩ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The process of donating blood was actually pretty simple.
entries.translation: Mũtaratara wa kũheana thakame waarĩ mũhũthũ mũno.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: We both filled out a questionnaire and answered some questions about our health history.
entries.translation: Ithuerĩ nĩ twacokirie mũtaratara wa ciũria na ciũria igũrũ rĩa rũgano rwitũ rwa ũgima wa mwĩrĩ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Then, we had our blood pressure checked and our veins were checked to make sure they were big enough.
entries.translation: Tũgĩcoka, tũgĩthimũo kũhaica gwa thakame ciitũ na mĩcibi ya thakame ĩkĩrorũo kana yaarĩ mĩnene wega.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Once we were cleared to donate, we each sat down in a chair and had a needle inserted into our arms.
entries.translation: Twarekũo tũheane thakame, nĩ twaikarire thĩ gĩti-inĩ na cindano ĩgĩthecũo mokoi-inĩ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The blood was collected in a bag, and the whole process took about 15 minutes.
entries.translation: Thakame yekĩrirũo mũhuko-inĩ, na mũtaratara ũcio wothe warĩ wa dagĩka ta 15.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: It felt good to know that we were helping to save lives.
entries.translation: Twaiguire wega nĩ kũmenya atĩ nĩ twateithagia kũhonokia mĩoyo.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: After we donated, we were given a juice box and a cookie to help us recover.
entries.translation: Twarĩkia kũheana, twaheirũo maaĩ ma matunda na geki cia gũteithia gwĩcokia.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: We also received a thank-you card from the blood bank.
entries.translation: Ona nĩ twanyitire kadi ya ngatho kuma kũrĩ bengi ya thakame.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: I'm glad that Abel and I decided to donate blood.
entries.translation: Nĩdakena atĩ Abel na niĩ nĩtwatuire itua kũheana thakame.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: It was a quick and easy way to make a difference in the world.
entries.translation: Warĩ ũndũ wa naihenya na mũhũthũ kũgarũra bũrũri.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: I encourage everyone to consider donating blood if they are eligible.
entries.translation: Nĩdĩrekĩra o mũndũ o wothe hinya atue itua kũheana thakame angĩkorũo no ahote.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: It's a simple act of kindness that can help save lives.
entries.translation: Nĩ kaũndũ kahũthũ ga tha karĩa kangĩteithia kũhonokia mĩoyo.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: A solo traveler was found safe after spending two nights lost in the Swiss Alps.
entries.translation: Mũgendi ũmwe nĩ onekanire arĩ mwega thutha wa gũtinda matũkũ meerĩ oriire kũũrĩa Swiss Alps.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The 25-year-old woman, who has not been identified, was hiking in the mountains when she became separated from her group.
entries.translation: Mũtumia ũcio wa mĩaka 25, ũrĩa atarĩ aratambũrũo, ahaicaga irĩma icio rĩrĩa atigithanirio kuuma kũrĩ ngurubu yake.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: She was reported missing on Tuesday, and search teams were dispatched to find her.
entries.translation: Anĩrĩirũo nĩ orĩte kũrĩ mũthenya wa Jumaine, na ikundi cia gwetha cigĩtũmũo kũmwetha.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The woman was eventually found on Thursday, about 10 miles from where she had been hiking.
entries.translation: Mũthia-inĩ mũtumia ũcio nĩ onekanire kũrĩ mũthenya wa Alamithi, kĩndũ ta mairo 10 kuuma kũrĩa ahaicagĩra.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: She was cold and dehydrated, but otherwise in good condition.
entries.translation: Aarĩ na heho na mũng'aru, no ningĩ aarĩ o mwega.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: She told rescuers that she had been following a trail when she got turned around.
entries.translation: Erire ahonokia ake atĩ nĩ arumagĩrĩra njĩra rĩrĩa acokirio na thutha.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: She spent the night in a cave, and she survived by eating snow and drinking from a stream.
entries.translation: Ũtukũ ũcio akomire ngurunga-inĩ, na atũrĩre nĩ ũndũ wa kũrĩa mbarabu na kũnyua maaĩ ma karũũĩ-inĩ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The woman's experience is a reminder of the importance of being prepared when hiking in the mountains.
entries.translation: Ũndũ ũcio wa mũtumia nĩ kĩririkanio kĩa bata wa gũkorũo wĩharĩirie rĩrĩa ũrahaica irĩma-inĩ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Hikers should always bring a map, compass, and a flashlight, and they should tell someone where they are going and when they expect to return.
entries.translation: Ahaici hĩndĩ ciothe no mũhaka magakua mabu, kombasi, na toci, na no mũhaka makeera mũndũ kũrĩa marathiĩ na rĩrĩa maracokoroka.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: When I was a kid, I would spend hours poring over magazines.
entries.translation: Rĩrĩa darĩ mwana, nĩdahũthagĩra mathaa maingĩ gũthoma magathĩti.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: I would read every article, look at every picture, and cut out the ones I liked to put in my scrapbook.
entries.translation: Nĩdathomaga o gĩcunjĩ, ngarora o mbica, na gũtinia iria dedaga gwĩkĩra ibuku-inĩ rĩakwa rĩa tũcunjĩ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: I loved the way magazines could transport me to different worlds and make me think about things in new ways.
entries.translation: Nĩdedete ũrĩa magathĩti marĩ madware kũrĩ mabũrũri ngũrani na gũtũma dĩcirie na njĩra ingĩ njerũ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: One day, I was reading an article about brain science in a magazine.
entries.translation: Mũthenya ũmwe, nĩ dathomaga gĩcunjĩ kĩĩgiĩ ũhoro wa tombo ngathĩti-inĩ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The article was really interesting, and it made me think about how my brain works.
entries.translation: Gĩcunjĩ kĩũ kĩarĩ kĩega mũno, na gĩgĩtũma dĩcirie ũrĩa tombo wakwa ũrutaga wĩĩra.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: I realized that I could use my brain to learn anything I wanted, and that was an amazing feeling.
entries.translation: Ngĩmenya atĩ no hũthĩre tombo wakwa kũmenya o kĩrĩa ingĩenda, na atĩ nĩ kaũndũ kega mũno.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: I've been reading magazines ever since, and I still love the way they can open my mind to new ideas.
entries.translation: Ngoretũo ngĩthoma magathĩti kuma hĩndĩ ĩyo, na no nyendete ũrĩa mangĩhingũra meciria makwa kũrĩ maũndũ meerũ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The debate about whether animals are happier in the wild or in zoos is a complex one with no easy answers.
entries.translation: Ndeereti ya kana nyamũ nĩ ikenaga makĩria irĩ werũ-inĩ kana irĩ mũgũnda-inĩ wa nyamũ nĩ nditũ mũno na ĩria ĩtarĩ na anja cia raithi.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: There are many factors to consider, including the individual animal's needs, the type of zoo, and the quality of care provided.
entries.translation: Nĩ kũrĩ maũndũ maingĩ ma kũrora, o hamwe na mabataro na nyamũ kĩũmbe, mũhiano wa mũgũnda wa nyamũ, na ũtungati ũrĩa ũraheanũo.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Some animals, such as elephants, are highly social and need to interact with other elephants in order to thrive.
entries.translation: Nyamũ imwe, ta njogu, nĩ ciendete kũingĩrana na andũ mũno na nĩ cibataraga gũikarania na njogu iria ingĩ nĩ getha itheereme.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: In the wild, elephants live in herds of up to 100 individuals.
entries.translation: Kũu werũ-inĩ, njogu cikaraga makundi-inĩ ma nginyagia njogu 100.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: They spend their days foraging for food, playing, and socializing.
entries.translation: Cihũthagĩra mĩthenya yacio igĩetha irio, gũthaka, na kũingĩrana.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: In a zoo, elephants may not have the same opportunities to interact with other elephants, which can lead to boredom and frustration.
entries.translation: Mũgũnda-inĩ wa nyamũ, njogu itirĩ na twanya ta tũu twa kũingĩrana na njogu irĩa ingĩ, kũrĩa no kũrehe kuigua kũnoga na kũrakara.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Other animals, such as lions, are solitary hunters.
entries.translation: Nyamũ ingĩ, ta mĩrũthi, nĩ mĩgwĩmi ya nyamũ kĩũmbe.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: In the wild, lions live in prides of up to 15 individuals.
entries.translation: Kũu werũ-inĩ, mĩrũthi ĩikaraga ikundi-inĩ cia nginyagia mĩrũthi 15.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: However, each lion within the pride has its own territory and does not interact with other lions very often.
entries.translation: Ona kũrĩ o ũguo, o mũrũthi thĩiniĩ wa gĩkundi kĩayo nĩ ũrĩ na gĩcunjĩ kĩayo na ũtiingĩranaga na mĩrũthi ĩngĩ maita maingĩ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: In a zoo, lions may be able to live in larger enclosures with more space to roam, which can provide them with more opportunities to exercise and explore.
entries.translation: Mũgũnda-inĩ wa nyamũ, mĩrũthi no ĩhote gũikara icigo-inĩ nene hamwe na mũgũnda wa gũcangacanga, kũrĩa kũngĩcihe twanya tũingĩ twa mathoethi ona gũthuthuria.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The type of zoo also plays a role in the welfare of its animals.
entries.translation: Mũhiano wa mũgũnda wa nyamũ nĩ wa bata wega-inĩ wa nyamũ ciayo.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Some zoos are very large and provide their animals with spacious enclosures, while others are smaller and may not have as much space.
entries.translation: Mĩgũnda ĩmwe ya nyamũ nĩ mĩnene mũno na nĩ ĩheaga nyamũ coayo itego nene mũno, na iria ingi ni nini na no ciage gũkorwo na mũgũnda mũnene.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: As I'm driving down the road, I see a goat giving birth in the median.
entries.translation: Ngĩtwarithia ngari barabara-inĩ, ngona mbũri ĩgĩciara ya mũigana wa mĩaka.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: She's lying on her side and her two front legs are extended in front of her.
entries.translation: Akomeire mwene ũmwe na magũrũ make meerĩ ma mbere matambũrũkĩte mbere yake.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The baby goat is coming out of her right side and it's head is already visible.
entries.translation: Kaana kau ka mbũri karaumĩra mwena wake wa ũrĩo na kĩongo gĩako nĩ kĩronekana.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The mother goat looks up at me and I can see the fear in her eyes.
entries.translation: Mbũrĩ ĩyo ĩrandora na nĩ dĩrona guoya ĩa ũrĩ maitho-inĩ make.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: She's probably wondering if I'm going to hurt her or her baby.
entries.translation: No gũkorwo ararigũo kana nĩngũtihia kana gake.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: I stop the car and get out.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: I walk over to the goat and kneel down next to her.
entries.translation: Ngathiĩ harĩa mbũrĩ ĩrĩ na ngaturia ndu hakũhĩ nake.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: I gently stroke her head and tell her that everything is going to be okay.
entries.translation: Ngamũthathaya kahora na kũmwĩra atĩ maũndũ mothe nĩ mekwagĩra.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The baby goat starts to emerge and I can see that it's a little girl.
entries.translation: Kana ka mbũri gakambĩrĩria kuumĩra na nĩ dĩrona atĩ nĩ kairĩtu kanini.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: She's crying and her mother licks her clean.
entries.translation: Nĩ kararĩra na nyina agagacũna gathere.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: I watch as the mother goat and baby bond and I feel a sense of peace.
entries.translation: Ngerorera mbũri ĩkvmenyana na kana na ngaigua thayũ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The city was a vast, sprawling metropolis, full of life and energy.
entries.translation: Cĩtĩ ĩyo yaarĩ itũũra inene, itũũra rĩarahĩte, rĩihũire mũoyo na hinya.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: It was a place where anything was possible, and where dreams could come true.
entries.translation: Kwarĩ kũndũ kũrĩa mothe maarĩ mahoteke, na kũrĩa iroto ciarĩ ikinyanĩre.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: But for every person who found success in the city, there were many more who struggled to make ends meet.
entries.translation: No kũrĩ mũndũ o wothe ũrĩa wonaga ũgaacĩru itũũra-inĩ rĩu, nĩ kwarĩ na angĩ aingĩ arĩa mathĩĩnĩkaga kũhingia mabataro.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: These people lived in the slums, in tiny apartments that were often overcrowded and in disrepair.
entries.translation: Andũ aya matũũraga icagi-inĩ, tũnyũmba-inĩ tũnini tũrĩa maita maingĩ twarĩ na andũ aingĩ mũno na tũthũkangu.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: They worked long hours for low pay, and they often had to go without basic necessities like food and healthcare.
entries.translation: Nĩ marutaga wĩra mathaa maingĩ kwa marĩhi manini, na kaingĩ nĩ maagaga mabataro ma bata ta irio na dawa.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: One such person was a young woman named Amelia.
entries.translation: Mũndũ ũmwe ta ũcio aarĩ mũtumia mũnini wetagũo Amelia.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: She had come to the city with big dreams, but she quickly found that reality was much different than she had imagined.
entries.translation: Nĩ aarĩ okĩĩte itũũra-inĩ rĩũ na iroto nene, no nĩ amenyire ona ihenya atĩ ũũma waarĩ ngũrani mũno na ũrĩa eciiragia.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: She worked as a waitress in a small diner, and she could barely make enough money to pay her rent.
entries.translation: Arutaga wĩra ta mũruti wĩra wa mũkawa-inĩ kamũkawa-inĩ kanini, na onaga mbeca nini tu cia kũmũrĩhĩra nyũmba.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: She often went to bed hungry, and she was always worried about her future.
entries.translation: Kaingĩ nĩ akomaga arĩ mũhũtu, na nĩ amakaga hĩndĩ ciothe igũrũ rĩa matũkũ na hau mbere.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: One day, Amelia was walking home from work when she saw a man sitting on a bench.
entries.translation: Mũthenya ũmwe rĩ, Amelia athiaga mũciĩ kuuma wĩra-inĩ rĩrĩa onire mũndũ mũrũme aikarĩire gĩtĩ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: He was homeless, and he was holding a sign that said, "Will work for food." Amelia felt sorry for the man, and she decided to buy him a sandwich.
entries.translation: Daarĩ na gĩikaro, na nĩ anyitĩĩte kĩmenyithia kĩaugaga, "Ngũruta wĩĩra heo irio." Amelia nĩ amũigwĩrĩire tha, na agĩtua itua kũmũgũrĩra mũgate.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: As she was talking to the man, she learned that his name was Charlie.
entries.translation: Akĩaria na mũndũ mũrũme ũcio rĩ, akĩmenya atĩ etagwo Charlie.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Demonetization is the process of removing legal tender from circulation.
entries.translation: Kweheria mbeca nĩ mũtaratara wa kũruta kandarathi ya kĩwatho kuuma kũrĩ mũingĩ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: In India, Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced on November 8, 2016, that all ₹500 and ₹1000 banknotes would cease to be legal tender from midnight.
entries.translation: Kũũrĩa India, Prime Minister Narenda Modi nĩ anĩrĩire kũrĩ Novemba 8, 2016, atĩ mbeca ciothe cia maratathi cia ₹500 na ₹1000 nĩ igũtiga gũtwĩka kandarathi ya kĩwatho kwambĩrĩria thaa thita cia ũtukũ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: This move was intended to crack down on corruption and counterfeiting, but it also caused significant disruption and hardship for many people.
entries.translation: Itua rĩĩrĩ rĩarongoragia kũnina ungumania na ũthondeki wa indo cia maheni, no nĩ rĩarehire ũthũkia mũnene na mathĩna kũrĩ andũ aingĩ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: There are several reasons to be skeptical of demonetization.
entries.translation: Nĩ kũrĩ na itũmi nyingĩ cia kwaga kwĩhoka weheria wa mbeca.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: First, it is not clear that it will be effective in reducing corruption.
entries.translation: Wa mbere, tĩ ũndũ mũtherie atĩ nĩ ũkũhota kũnyihia ungumania.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Corruption is a complex problem that cannot be solved simply by removing cash from circulation.
entries.translation: Ungumania nĩ thĩĩna mũũru ũrĩa ũtangĩninwo na njĩra ya kweheria mbeca kũrĩ mũingĩ tu.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: In fact, there is some evidence that demonetization may actually increase corruption, as it makes it more difficult for people to track and trace their money.
entries.translation: Ũũma nĩ atĩ, nĩ kũrĩ na ũira mũnini atĩ weheria wa mbeca no wongerere ungumania, tondũ nĩ ũritũhagĩra andũ aingĩ kũhota gũkinyithia na kũona mbeca ciao.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Second, demonetization is likely to have a negative impact on the poor.
entries.translation: Keerĩ, weheria wa mbeca no ũrehe maimĩrĩra mooru kũrĩ athĩĩni.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Many poor people in India rely on cash for their daily transactions.
entries.translation: Andũ aingĩ arĩa athĩĩni kũũrĩa India mehokaga mbeca baribari cia mahũthĩro ma o mũthenya.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The sudden withdrawal of large-denomination banknotes made it difficult for them to buy food, pay their bills, and access other essential services.
entries.translation: Kũrutũo kwa naihenya kwa mbeca nene cia maratathi nĩ gwatũmire kũmaritũhĩre kũgũra irio, kũrĩha mahũthĩro mao, na kũgĩa na matungata mangĩ ma bata.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Third, demonetization has caused significant disruption to the economy.
entries.translation: Gatatũ, kweheria mbeca nĩ kũrehete ũthũkia mũnene kũrĩ ũtonga wao.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Businesses had to close for days or even weeks while they adjusted to the new currency.
entries.translation: Biathara nĩ ciahingirũo thikũ ona ciumia nyingĩ rĩrĩa mamenyeraga mbeca icio njerũ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The dish is said to have originated in the Philippines, where it is known as lechon.
entries.translation: Irio icio ciĩrikaga ciaumire kũũrĩa Philippines, kũrĩa ciũĩkaine ta lechon.

entries.english: It is also popular in other parts of Southeast Asia, such as Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand.
entries.translation: Nĩ ciendetũo mũno mĩena mĩngĩ ya Southeast Asia, ta Indonesia, Malaysia, na Thailand.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: To make lechon, a whole pig is gutted and cleaned, then stuffed with a mixture of garlic, ginger, lemongrass, and other spices.
entries.translation: Gũthondeka lechon, ngũrũe ng'ima ĩrutagũo nyongo na gũthambio, ĩgacoka ĩgatũndĩrũo mũtukanio wa gĩtũngũrũ thaumu, lemongrass, na indo ingĩ cia kũruga.

entries.english: The pig is then roasted over a fire of charcoal or wood for several hours.

entries.english: The result is a juicy, flavorful meat that is perfect for a special occasion.

entries.english: Santiago, an old Cuban fisherman, has gone eighty-four days without catching a fish.
entries.translation: Santiago, mũtegi thamaki mũkũrũ wa Cuba, nĩ aikarĩte thikũ mĩrongo ĩnana na inya atanyitĩte thamaki ona ĩmwe.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: He is the oldest man in the village, and the youngest, Manolin, no longer wants to fish with him because the old man is unlucky.
entries.translation: Nĩwe mũthuuri ũrĩa mũkũrũ mũno itũũra-inĩ, nake ũrĩa mũnini mũno, Manolin, darenda rĩngĩ gũtega thamaki nake tondũ mũthuuri ũcio mũkũrũ darĩ na mũnyaka.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: One day, Santiago sets out in his skiff and hooks a giant marlin.
entries.translation: Mũthenya ũmwe rĩ, Santiago agathiĩ na gatarũ gake na akahocia gĩthamaki kĩnene.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The marlin is so big that it pulls the skiff far out to sea.
entries.translation: Gĩthamaki kĩũ nĩ kĩnene mũno nginya gĩkagucia gatarũ kũu iria-inĩ makĩria.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Santiago fights the marlin for two days and nights, but he cannot bring it in.
entries.translation: Santiago akarũa na gĩthamaki kĩu mĩthenya ĩĩrĩ na dukũ igĩrĩ, no daigana gũkĩhota.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The marlin is too heavy, and the old man is too tired.
entries.translation: Gĩthamaki kĩu nĩ kĩritũ mũno, nake mũthuuri ũcio mũkũrũ nĩ mũnogu mũno.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Finally, the marlin begins to tire.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Santiago is able to get a harpoon into the marlin, and he kills it.
entries.translation: Santiago akahota gũtheeca gĩthamaki kĩu na kĩgũtha, na agakĩũraga.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: But the marlin is so big that Santiago cannot bring it into the boat.
entries.translation: No gĩthamaki nĩ kĩnene mũno na Santiago akaremũo nĩ gũkĩingĩria gatarũ-inĩ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: He ties the marlin to the side of the boat and begins to row back to shore.
entries.translation: Akoherera gĩthamaki kĩũ mwena-inĩ ũmwe wa gatarũ na akambia gũtwarithia gatarũ rũteere-inĩ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: A school of sharks follows the boat, and they begin to eat the marlin.
entries.translation: Gĩkundi ĩa thamaki nene gĩkauma gatarũ thuutha, na ikambia kũrĩa gĩthamaki kĩu kĩnene.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Santiago fights the sharks off, but he cannot stop them all.
entries.translation: Santiago akaingata thamaki icio nene, na daigana kũgirĩrĩria ciothe.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: By the time he reaches shore, only the head and the tail of the marlin are left.
entries.translation: Rĩrĩa arakinya rũteere-inĩ rĩ, no kĩongo tu na mũthia wa gĩthamaki itigarĩte.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The police will likely take the person to the station and question him.
entries.translation: Kwahoteka borithi nĩmegũtwara mũndũ ũcio ceceni-inĩ nĩgetha mamũhunge mahũri.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: They will want to know where he got the wallet and why he was carrying it.
entries.translation: No mende kũmenya kũrĩa ararutire kĩbeti na gĩtumi gĩa gũgĩkuua.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: If the person cannot provide a satisfactory explanation, he may be arrested and charged with theft.
entries.translation: Mũndũ ũcio angĩaga kũheana gĩtumi kĩiganu, no aikio ngono na athitangwo na ciira wa ũici.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: If the person is arrested, he will be taken to jail and held until his trial.
entries.translation: Mũndũ ũcio aikio ngono, agatwarwo njera ahingĩrwo nginyagia mũthenya wa ciira.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: At his trial, the prosecution will have to prove beyond a reasonable doubt that he is guilty of theft.
entries.translation: Nakuo igooti-inĩ, no mũhaka mwena wa thitango wonanie na ma hatarĩ ngaja atĩ mũndũ ũcio ena ihĩtia rĩa kũiya.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The defense will have the opportunity to present evidence and witnesses that may help to exonerate the person.
entries.translation: Mũthitangwo nake aheo mweke wa kũruta ũira na aira arĩa mangĩteithĩrĩria kũmwohorithia.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: If the person is found guilty, he may be sentenced to jail time, probation, or community service.
entries.translation: Angĩonekana na mahĩtia-rĩ, mũndũ ũcio no atuirwo kĩoho kĩa njera, kĩoho kĩa nja, kana gũtungata mũingĩ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: He may also be ordered to pay restitution to the victim of the theft.
entries.translation: Nĩngĩ no athwo arĩhe mũndũ ũria aiyiire.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: In some cases, the person may be able to avoid criminal charges by entering into a diversion program.
entries.translation: Rĩmwe na rĩmwe, mũndũ ũcio no ahote kwĩgita ndagatwiruo na njĩra ya kũingĩra tabarĩra-inĩ ya kũgarura mĩtugo.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Diversion programs are designed to help people who have committed minor crimes avoid the criminal justice system.
entries.translation: Tabarĩra cia kũgarura mĩtugo ithondeketwo nĩguo gũteithĩrĩria andũ arĩa mekĩte tũmahĩtia tũnini nĩ getha matigatuĩrwo nĩ igooti.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: In a diversion program, the person may be required to complete community service, pay restitution, or attend counseling.
entries.translation: Tabarira-inĩ ĩyo ya kũgarura mĩtugo, mũndũ no arute wĩra wa gũtungatĩra mũingĩ, arĩhe mũndũ ũrĩa ahĩtĩirie, kana aingĩre tabarĩra-inĩ ya mootaro.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: If the person is found not guilty, he will be released from jail and the charges against him will be dropped.
entries.translation: Mũndũ ũcio angĩonekana atĩ ndarĩ na ihĩtia, nĩ arekagĩrĩrio kuuma njera na mahĩtia maake makeherio.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: He will be able to go on with his life without a criminal record.
entries.translation: Akahoota gũtwarithia maica maake na mbere atarĩ na rekondi ya wĩkinai.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: It is important to note that the above is just a general overview of what may happen to a presumed thief who is held by police.
entries.translation: Nĩ wega kũririkana atĩ maũndũ macio marĩ hau iguru no matemo na njĩra nguhĩ ma makinya marĩa mũndũ wĩkuĩrwo na ũici angĩgerera moko-inĩ ma borithi.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The specific circumstances of each case will vary, and the outcome may depend on a number of factors, such as the evidence available, the person's criminal history, and the judge or jury's decision.
entries.translation: Mĩtaratara ya maciira ngũrani ndĩhanaine na maũmĩrĩra maringanaga na maũndũ mwanya mwanya, ta ũira ũrĩa ũrutĩtwo, historĩ ya wĩkinaĩ ya mũndũ na itua rĩa Mũcirithania kana janji.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The couple, a renowned linguist and a world-renowned pastry chef, had been trying for a baby for years.
entries.translation: Mũthuri umwe na mũtumia wake, ũmwe arĩ mũtaaramu wa thiomi na ũcio ũngĩ mũrugi wa mĩgate wĩ gatũ, makoretwo makĩgeria kũgĩa mwana mĩaka mĩingĩ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: They had been to every doctor and specialist they could find, but nothing seemed to work.
entries.translation: Makoretwo magĩthii kũrĩ mandagĩtarĩ na ataaramu aingĩ, no gũtiarĩ na ũmithio.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The linguist was starting to lose hope, and the pastry chef was worried that their reputation would be ruined if they couldn't have a child.
entries.translation: Mũtaaramu ũcio wa thiomi akĩanjia gũkua ngoro, na mũrugi wa mĩgate nĩ amakaga atĩ ngumo yao nĩ ĩgũthuka mangĩaga kũgĩa mwana.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: One day, the linguist was working on a new translation of a difficult poem when he had a breakthrough.
entries.translation: Mũthenya ũmwe-rĩ, mũtaaramu ũcio wa thiomi ataũraga irebeta iritũ na akĩigua aheo icookio.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: He realized that the key to having a child was to find a way to combine their two passions.
entries.translation: Akĩmenya atĩ njĩra njega ya kũgia mwana nĩ kũrehe hamwe maũndũ marĩa ngoro ciao cieri ciendete mũno.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: He called the pastry chef and told her his idea.

entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The pastry chef was skeptical at first, but she agreed to give it a try.

entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: They spent the next few months working on a new recipe for a cake that would be infused with the linguist's love of language and the pastry chef's love of baking.

entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: When the cake was finally finished, they took it to the premier of a new play that the linguist was translating.

entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: They waited until the after-party, and then they cut the cake and served it to everyone.

entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Everyone loved the taste, and they were all impressed by the story behind it.

entries.english: However, such knowledge is not mine to give.

entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Suffice it to say that my greatest dread is something so insidious and far-reaching that it defies description.

entries.english: It is a terror that lurks in the shadows, waiting to pounce at the most unexpected moment.

entries.english: It is a predator that feeds on my very essence, leaving me feeling weak and vulnerable.

entries.english: This insidious fear has been with me for as long as I can remember.

entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: It has shaped my life in ways that I am only beginning to understand.

entries.english: The influences of religion on music are vast and varied.
entries.translation: Ndini nĩ ĩhutagia nyĩmbo na njĩra nene mũno.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: From the chanting of hymns in ancient temples to the soaring melodies of gospel songs, music has long been used to express religious beliefs and emotions.
entries.translation: Rĩngĩ nĩ andũ makĩina nyĩmbo cia tene hekarũ-inĩ kana mĩgambo ya andũ makĩina nyĩmbo cia kũgooca, andũ matũrĩte mahũthĩrĩte nyĩmbo kũonania mawĩtĩkio mao na maũndũ marĩa marĩ ngoro-inĩ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: In many religions, music is seen as a way to connect with the divine.
entries.translation: Thĩĩnĩ wa ndini nyingi-rĩ, nyĩmbo cioyagwo ta njĩra ya kwĩnyitithania na ũrĩa mũtheru.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The sounds and rhythms of music can create a sense of awe and reverence, and can help to transport the listener to a higher plane of consciousness.
entries.translation: Mĩgambo na mĩrurumo ya nyĩmbo no ĩtũme andũ maigue ta mararongoria kana gũtĩĩya, na no ĩmateithie kũigua ta maracemania na kĩũndũ kĩa na thĩĩnĩ kana gĩa kĩrooho mũno.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: For example, in Hinduism, music is considered to be a form of yoga.
entries.translation: Kwa mũhiano, thĩĩnĩ wa ndini ya Kĩĩhĩndĩ, nyĩmbo cioyagwo ta njĩra ya gwĩka yoga.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The practice of kirtan, or devotional chanting, is said to help to purify the mind and open the heart to the divine.
entries.translation: Miĩaratara ya kirtan, kana kũina na mĩgambo ya gũthathaiya, ĩrĩkanaga nĩ ĩteithagia gũtheria meciria na kũhingurĩra ũrĩa mũtheru ngoro-inĩ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: In Buddhism, music is often used as a form of meditation, helping to focus the mind and bring about a state of calm and tranquility.
entries.translation: Thĩĩnĩ wa ũrutani wa dini ya Buddha, nyĩmbo ĩhuthagĩrwo ta njĩra ya kũrehe meciria marikĩru, na gũteithia kũhoreria meciria na kũgĩa na thayũ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: In addition to its spiritual role, music can also be used to address social and political issues.
entries.translation: Hamwe na maũndũ macio ma kĩroho, nyĩmbo no ihũthĩrwo gũteithĩrĩria maũndũ megĩĩ mũingĩ na ũteti.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: In the civil rights movement, for example, music played a powerful role in mobilizing people and inspiring them to fight for justice.
entries.translation: Hĩndĩ ya mũrurumo wa gũtetera ihooto cia mũingĩ, nyĩmbo ciarĩ njvra njega ya kũigwithia andũ marũĩrĩre kĩhooto.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The songs of Martin Luther King Jr, Mahalia Jackson, and others helped to give voice to the hopes and dreams of African Americans, and helped to bring about a more just and equitable society.
entries.translation: Nyĩmbo cia Martin Luther King Jr, Mahalia Jackson, na angĩ aingĩ nĩ ciateithirie kũrehe mwĩhoko kũrĩ aikari a Amerika arĩa mena kĩhumo kĩa Afrika, na igĩteithia kũrehe kĩhooto na ũiganania wa andũ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The peacock is a large and colorful bird that is native to Asia.
entries.translation: Tauthi nĩ nyoni nene na thaka mũno ĩrĩa kĩhumo kĩayo nĩ Asia.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: It is known for its beautiful plumage, which is made up of iridescent blue, green, and purple feathers.
entries.translation: Yũuĩkaine mũno nĩ ũndũ wa mathagu mayo mathaka, marĩa makoragwo na rangi wa biruiru, ngirini na papũ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Peacocks are also known for their elaborate courtship displays, which they perform to attract mates.
entries.translation: Ningĩ tauthi nĩ ciũĩkaine nĩ ũndũ wa mĩtugo yacio ya mwanya, ya kũgucĩrĩria nyoni cĩa mwera.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: During these displays, the male peacock will spread his tail feathers and fan them out to create a large, colorful fan.
entries.translation: Gĩtiribu gĩkĩ-rĩ, tauthi ya njamba yambararagia mathagu mayo ma thutha magathondeka gĩtarũrũ kĩnene gĩthaka.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The female peacock will then choose a mate based on the size and beauty of his tail feathers.
entries.translation: Tauthi ya mwera nayo ĩgacagũra njamba kũringana na mũigana na ũthaka wa mathagu mayo.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Peacocks are also known for their intelligence and ability to learn.
entries.translation: Ningĩ tauthi nĩ ciũĩkaine nĩ ũndũ wa ũũgĩ wacio na ũhooti wa kwĩruta maũndũ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: They can be trained to perform tricks and can even be taught to talk.
entries.translation: No ibundithio gwĩka tũmaũndũ twa mwanya na nginya kwaria.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: In addition to their beauty and intelligence, peacocks are also important members of the ecosystem.
entries.translation: Hamwe na ũũgĩ na ũthaka wacio-rĩ, tauthi nĩ nyamũ cia bata harĩ maũndũ marĩa matũrigicĩirie.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: They help to control the population of insects and other pests, and their droppings can help to fertilize the soil.
entries.translation: Nĩ iteithagia kũiganania mũigana wa tũtambi na tũrĩa nime, na maai macio nĩ mateithagia kũnoria tĩĩri.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Then I turn it over and begin to write "Dearest Ted," I write. "I'm having the time of my life here in Italy.
entries.translation: Ngacooka ngamĩgarũra mwena ũcio ũngĩ na ngaambĩrĩria kwandĩka "Mwendwa wakwa Ted," ngathie na mbere kwandĩka, "Nĩndĩrakenera mũno ũikaro wakwa gũkũ Italy.

entries.english: The weather is perfect, the food is delicious, and the people are so friendly.

entries.english: The history of Cameroon is long and complex, dating back to the earliest human settlements in the region.
entries.translation: Histori ya bũrũri wa Cameroon nĩ ndaihũ na nĩ nene, kuuma o hĩndi ya aikari a mbere biũ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The area was first settled by Bantu peoples around 3000 BCE, and it was later conquered by the Kanem-Bornu Empire in the 11th century.
entries.translation: Andũ a mbere guũikara gĩcigo kĩu maarĩ a mũhĩrĩga wa Bantu ta mĩaka 3000 BCE, waathani wa Kanem-Bornu ũgĩcooka ũkĩoerera karine-inĩ ya 11.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: In the 15th century, the Portuguese arrived in Cameroon and established trade relations with the local people.
entries.translation: Thĩĩnĩ wa karine ya 15, Portuguese magĩkinya Cameroon na makĩambĩrĩria ndũgũ cia mbiacara na andũ a kũu.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The region was later colonized by Germany in the 1880s, and it became a German colony known as Kamerun.
entries.translation: Thũtha-inĩ gĩcigo kĩu gĩkĩingĩra waathani-inĩ wa Njirimani mĩaka-inĩ ya 1880, na gĩgituika gĩcigo kĩa Njirimani gĩetagwo Kamerun.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: During World War I, Cameroon was occupied by British and French forces, and it was divided between the two countries after the war.
entries.translation: Hĩndĩ ya Mbara ya Mbere ya Thi, waathani wa Camerun ũkĩoywo nĩ mbirarũ cia Ngeretha na Faranja, na ĩkĩgayanio gatagatĩ ka mabũrũri macio meerĩ mbara yathira.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The British-controlled region became known as Southern Cameroons, while the French-controlled region became known as French Cameroon.
entries.translation: Gĩcigo kĩrĩa gĩathagwo nĩ Ngeretha gĩgĩtwo Cameroon ya Mũhuro, na kĩrĩa gĩathagwo nĩ Faranja gĩgĩtwo Cameroon ya Faranja.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: In 1960, Southern Cameroons became independent from Britain, and it merged with French Cameroon to form the Federal Republic of Cameroon.
entries.translation: Mwaka-inĩ wa 1960, Cameroon ya Mũhuro ĩkiuma waathani-ini wa Ngeretha na ĩkiungana na Cameroon ya Faranja gũthondeka Federal Republic of Cameroon.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: In 1972, the federal system was abolished and Cameroon became a unitary state.
entries.translation: Mwaka-inĩ wa 1972, mũũngano wa mabũruri ũkininwo na Cameroon ĩgĩtuĩka bũrũri wa thirikari ĩmwe.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Cameroon has experienced a number of political and economic challenges in recent years.
entries.translation: Kwa ihinda rĩa mĩaka mĩnini mĩhĩtũku, bũrũri wa Cameroon nĩ ũkoretwo na moritũ maingĩ ma gĩũteti na ma kĩĩmbeca.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Mystery surrounds disappearance of Eva Green.
entries.translation: Ũhooro wa kũũra kwa Eva Green nĩ wa kiriga mũno.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Eva Green, a 25-year-old woman from London, has been missing for over a week.
entries.translation: Eva Green, mũirĩtu wa mĩaka 25 kuuma London, ndaramenyeka kũrĩa arĩ kwa ihinda rĩa kiumia kĩmwe rĩũ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: She was last seen on February 25th, leaving her apartment in the city's Notting Hill neighborhood.
entries.translation: Onekanĩre rĩa mũico tarĩki 25 mweri wa keerĩ, akiuma gwake nyũmba itũũra-inĩ rĩa Notting Hill.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Green is described as being 5'6" tall, with long brown hair and green eyes.
entries.translation: Green nĩ wa ũraihu wa fiti ithano na inji ĩthathatũ, na nĩarĩ njwirĩ ndaihu ya rangi wa gĩĩtĩri na maitho ma ngirini.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: She was last seen wearing a black coat, jeans, and a white t-shirt.
entries.translation: Rĩa mũico ekĩrĩte igoti rĩirũ, jinsi na shati ya rangi mwerũ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Police have said that they are concerned for Green's safety and are asking anyone with information about her whereabouts to come forward.
entries.translation: Borithi nĩ maũgĩte atĩ nĩ maramakio nĩ ũgitĩri wa Green na makooria mũndũ o wothe ũngĩkorwo na ndũmĩrĩri ĩgie kũrĩa angĩkorwo eyumĩrie.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Green's family and friends are desperate for news of her.
entries.translation: Bamĩrĩ na arata a Green nĩ metereire mũno kũigua ndũmĩrĩri.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: They have been posting flyers and distributing missing person's posters around the city.
entries.translation: Makoretwo magĩkĩra ibandĩko na gũthiũrũrukia maratathi ma mũndũ ũũrĩte.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: They have also set up a Facebook page to help spread the word about her disappearance.
entries.translation: Oho nĩ mahingũrĩte rũrenda rwa Facebook rwa gũteithĩrĩria gũtheremia ũhoro wa kũũra gwake.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The police have not yet released any information about possible suspects or motives in Green's disappearance.
entries.translation: Borithi matirĩ mararekereria ndũmĩrĩri o yothe ĩgie ekũĩrwo kana itũmi iria ingĩkorwo ĩkũrũhanĩte na kũũra kwa Green.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: They are asking anyone with information to come forward, no matter how small.
entries.translation: Nĩ maroria mũndũ o wothe ũngĩkorwo na ndũmĩrĩri eyumĩrie, o na angĩkorwo nĩ ndũmĩrĩri nini.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Green's disappearance is a mystery, but her family and friends are hopeful that she will be found safe and sound.
entries.translation: Kũũra kwa Green nĩ kĩriga, no bamĩrĩ na arata ake mena mwĩhoko atĩ nĩ akwoneka arĩ na thayũ na ũgima mwega wa mwĩrĩ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Trimming your dog's nails is a necessary part of grooming, but it can be a daunting task for some pet owners.
entries.translation: Kũrenga ndwara cia ngui yaku nĩ gwa bata harĩ kũmenyerera ũther, no ti wira mũhũthũ kũrĩ andũ amwe arĩa maigaga ngui.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: If you're not sure how to trim your dog's nails, don't worry - it's easier than you think.
entries.translation: Angĩkorwo ndũrĩ na ũũma wa ũrĩa ũngĩrenga ndwara cia ngui yaku-rĩ, ndũkamake - nĩ ũndũ mũhũthũ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The first step is to gather your supplies.
entries.translation: Ikinya rĩa mbere nĩ gũcokanĩrĩria indo irĩa ũrabatara.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: You'll need a pair of sharp scissors or a nail clipper, a styptic powder or pencil, and a towel.
entries.translation: Ũgũbatara magathĩ moogĩ kana kanyamu ga kũrenga ndwara, mũtutu wa kũrigĩrĩria kuura thakame, na taurũ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Next, you'll need to clip your dog's nails in a comfortable place.
entries.translation: Thutha ũcio, nĩ ũgũbatara kũrengera ndwara cia ngui yaku handũ hahoreru.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: If your dog is nervous, try clipping their nails in a quiet room where they can't see out the window.
entries.translation: Ngui yaku ĩngĩnyitwo nĩ guoya-rĩ, geria kũrengera ndwara ciayo rumu-inĩ ĩtarĩ na inegene, handũ ĩtaronera ndirica-inĩ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: You may also want to have someone help you hold your dog still.
entries.translation: Ningĩ no ũkorwo na mũndũ ũragũteithia kũnyita ngui yaku.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: To trim your dog's nails, start by gently grasping their paw.
entries.translation: Nĩ getha ũrenge ndwara cia ngui yaku, ambĩrĩria na kũnyita ndwara ciayo.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Then, use your scissors or clippers to clip the tip of the nail.
entries.translation: Thutha ũcio, hũthĩra magathĩ kana kanyamũ ga kũrenga ndwara gũtinĩria igũrũ.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Be careful not to cut too short, as this can cause pain and bleeding.
entries.translation: Wĩhũge ndũkarenge mũno, nĩ tondũ no ĩigue ruo kana yuure thakame.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: If you do cut your dog's nail too short, apply a styptic powder or pencil to stop the bleeding.
entries.translation: Angĩkorwo nĩ warenga ndwara cia ngui yaku ciakũhĩha mũno, haka mũtutu wa kũgirĩrĩria kuura thakame.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Styptic powders and pencils are available at most pet stores.
entries.translation: Mĩtutu ya kũgirĩrĩria kuura thakame nĩ yonekanaga matuka-inĩ maingĩ ma indo cia nyamu cia mũcii.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Once you've trimmed all of your dog's nails, be sure to reward them with a treat.
entries.translation: Warĩkia kũrenga ndwara ciothe cia ngui yaku, ririkana kũmihe kĩheo.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Trimming nails can be a stressful experience for some dogs, so it's important to make it a positive experience.
entries.translation: Ngui nyingĩ no cĩĩtigĩre kũrengwo ndwara, kogwo he bata gũtigĩrĩra atĩ nĩwathondeka handũ heega hahoreru.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: With a little practice, you'll be able to trim your dog's nails like a pro.
entries.translation: Ũngĩmenyera kũrengaga ndwara cia ngui yaku, no ũhoote gwĩkaga ũguo ta mũtaaramu.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_ki, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: And your dog will be happy to have their nails trimmed, too!
